elements.name: Technology & Digital Maturity
elements.aiAnswer: Technology investments are concentrated at subsidiary level with varying degrees of maturity. Stoelzle Glass Group is making 'substantial investments to significantly enhance the level of electrification in our glass production processes and maximise the efficient utilisation of waste heat' **[<460,019dc4cb-bfdf-71cf-acd2-bb8f4cba8dc1>]**. Stoelzle participates in the ZeroCO2Glas research project with 'a total project volume of approx. EUR 14.94 million' aimed at developing 'a revolutionary glass melting process in connection with a new type of CO2-neutral and energy saving glass melting furnace' with 'innovative melting technology aimed to reduce energy consumption by 15% compared to conventional furnaces' **[<457,019dc4cb-bfdc-7bfe-940f-3f63e0555127>]**. By autumn 2023, Stoelzle planned to have 'the first electric feeder in operation at its Austrian amber glass furnace, what makes Stoelzle a role model for all European glass makers' **[<459,019dc4cb-bfde-7fe5-87a6-4f6ff6462161>]**. Neuman Aluminium employs 'high-tech product systems for highly automated production' and has capabilities in manufacturing ADAS components including 'sensor housings, radar and camera housings, lidar components' **[<462,019dc4cb-b976-7c6b-8b97-13018e25dc10>]**. The Neuman Group has a dedicated Chief Information Officer (Robert Nährer) **[<420,019dc4cb-8f31-7c94-b0ce-ab74022f8773>]**. PREFA offers digital customer tools including an online configurator and digital services platform **[<441,019dc4cb-b780-76d2-bd3b-71f1d3077765>, <485,019dc4cb-ea3c-7ad6-9ca1-d370dc3a5651>]**. Stoelzle's CEO states 'Significant investments in R&D, state-of-the-art-technologies and expert staff are our key to future success' **[<458,019dc4cb-bfdd-7293-9a01-21bc84cc2589>]**. However, the CAG Holding itself 'verzichtet sogar darauf, eine eigene Website zu betreiben' (does not even maintain its own website) **[<433,019dc4cb-c636-7d31-b317-78a26b2d2656>]**, and no consolidated digital transformation roadmap, group-wide ERP system, or data analytics/AI strategy was identified.
elements.evidenceQuote: The overall goal of the ZeroCO2Glas project is to use an all-encompassing approach to develop a revolutionary glass melting process in connection with a new type of CO2-neutral and energy saving glass melting furnace. The project is funded by the German Ministry for Economy and Climate, BMWK, with a maximum of EUR 8.38 million with a total project volume of approx. EUR 14.94 million. **[<457,019dc4cb-bfdc-7bfe-940f-3f63e0555127>]**
elements.scoreRationale: Technology investments are evident in production processes but digital transformation maturity at the holding level is unclear. Stoelzle is investing in electrification of glass production with the first electric feeder operational in autumn 2023 **[<459,019dc4cb-bfde-7fe5-87a6-4f6ff6462161>]**, and participates in the ZeroCO2Glas research project (EUR 14.94 million total volume) for revolutionary glass melting technology **[<457,019dc4cb-bfdc-7bfe-940f-3f63e0555127>]**. Neuman Aluminium employs 'high-tech product systems for highly automated production' **[<462,019dc4cb-b976-7c6b-8b97-13018e25dc10>]** and has a dedicated CIO (Robert Nährer) **[<420,019dc4cb-8f31-7c94-b0ce-ab74022f8773>]**. PREFA offers digital tools like an online configurator and digital services platform **[<441,019dc4cb-b780-76d2-bd3b-71f1d3077765>]**. However, no evidence of a consolidated digital transformation roadmap, ERP system, data analytics/AI capabilities, or IT infrastructure strategy at the holding level was found. The CAG Holding does not even maintain its own website **[<433,019dc4cb-c636-7d31-b317-78a26b2d2656>]**, suggesting limited digital presence at the holding level.
elements.dataGap: No consolidated digital transformation roadmap, group-wide ERP or IT infrastructure strategy, data analytics/AI capabilities assessment, or digital maturity scorecard available at the holding level.

elements.name: Supply Chain & Partnerships
elements.aiAnswer: CAG Holding's supply chain spans a global manufacturing network. Neuman Aluminium Group 'produces in 10 facilities in 5 countries with more than 2,500 employees in Europe, North America and Asia' **[<420,019dc4cb-8f31-7c94-b0ce-ab74022f8773>]** and maintains 'intensive cooperation with automotive manufacturers and suppliers' including BMW, having produced 'several million battery pressure plates and tie rods annually for the BMW i3' since 2013 **[<469,019dc4cb-b97d-795a-8cf7-58feb42ffb76>]**. Stoelzle Glass Group operates '6 production sites in Austria, Great Britain, France, Czech Republic, Poland and USA' with '4 decoration sites' **[<484,019dc4cb-ea3b-725f-9d9a-58f192eac0e6>]**, and has developed the 'Glasy' recycling technology with Brantner green solutions to 'recover glass from residues of residual waste incineration with a purity of 99.9999%' **[<456,019dc4cb-bfdb-7156-a1ec-0e9dde5cc2b0>]**. TUBEX Group expanded through acquisition of Hungarian manufacturer Matrametal, with Dr. Grupp stating 'The acquisition of Matrametal complements the strategic orientation of the TUBEX Group in terms of location, customers and market' **[<471,019dc4cb-e9e3-7ca6-a5f1-0f52392da5a0>]**, bringing total capacity to '700 million aerosol cans and 1.6 billion aluminium tubes' across 7 production sites **[<471,019dc4cb-e9e3-7ca6-a5f1-0f52392da5a0>]**. Neuman Aluminium's operational strengths include 'a reliable supply chain through a strategic selection of suppliers and superior problem solving competence through systematic analysis' **[<461,019dc4cb-b975-706d-8ecc-bc84c2e4a97b>]**. Stoelzle participates in the International Partners in Glass Research (IPGR) consortium **[<457,019dc4cb-bfdc-7bfe-940f-3f63e0555127>]**. Neuman collaborates with 'the University of Leoben, Vienna University of Technology and ACT²' **[<468,019dc4cb-b97c-711d-9c0f-0cfd36786caa>]**. However, no formal supply chain risk assessment, dependency mapping, or resilience strategy documentation was found at the holding level.
elements.evidenceQuote: Other key strengths for the company include the consistent implementation of automotive standards in accordance with ISO/TS 16949; this results in high process quality delivered through proven standards, strict project control at new production or technological changes, preventative error management, a reliable supply chain through a strategic selection of suppliers and superior problem solving competence through systematic analysis. **[<461,019dc4cb-b975-706d-8ecc-bc84c2e4a97b>]**
elements.scoreRationale: The group demonstrates a vertically integrated supply chain across aluminium and glass value chains with global production footprint. Neuman Aluminium operates across 10 facilities in 5 countries **[<420,019dc4cb-8f31-7c94-b0ce-ab74022f8773>]** with intensive cooperation with automotive OEMs including BMW **[<469,019dc4cb-b97d-795a-8cf7-58feb42ffb76>]**. Stoelzle has 6 production sites across Europe and the USA **[<484,019dc4cb-ea3b-725f-9d9a-58f192eac0e6>]**. TUBEX recently acquired Matrametal in Hungary to complement its strategic orientation **[<471,019dc4cb-e9e3-7ca6-a5f1-0f52392da5a0>]**. However, no formal supply chain risk assessment, single-point-of-failure analysis, or supplier diversification strategy was documented. The group's dependence on aluminium and energy-intensive glass production creates inherent supply chain vulnerabilities. Neuman mentions 'a reliable supply chain through a strategic selection of suppliers' **[<461,019dc4cb-b975-706d-8ecc-bc84c2e4a97b>]** but details are not available.
elements.dataGap: No formal supply chain risk assessment, single-point-of-failure analysis, supplier concentration metrics, or supply chain resilience strategy documented at the holding level. Aluminium and energy price exposure risk quantification is missing.

elements.name: Innovation Capability
elements.aiAnswer: Innovation capability is a clear strength across CAG Holding subsidiaries. PREFA achieved a 'großer Meilenstein' (major milestone) with the 'innovative PREFA Solardachplatte' (solar roof tile) combining 'das bewährte PREFA Dachsystem mit integrierten Photovoltaik-Elementen' (the proven PREFA roof system with integrated photovoltaic elements) **[<485,019dc4cb-ea3c-7ad6-9ca1-d370dc3a5651>]**. The solar roof tile features 'state-of-the-art half-cell technology for maximally optimised performance' and is 'hail- and break-proof, storm-proof and rust-proof' **[<444,019dc4cb-b783-723b-861d-a5849e1f8bfd>]**. Neuman Aluminium operates a structured open innovation program: 'New ideas are generated through industry contacts, research institutes, innovation competitions and co-creation projects and evaluated in a structured innovation management system' with partnerships including 'the University of Leoben, Vienna University of Technology and ACT²' **[<468,019dc4cb-b97c-711d-9c0f-0cfd36786caa>]**. Neuman has a dedicated Head of Innovation (Annika Hämmerle) **[<419,019dc4cb-8f30-71a0-9a96-ed95306be90c>, <489,019dc4cb-ea40-7afe-9684-159e0bc3e5e4>]**. Stoelzle participates in the ZeroCO2Glas project (EUR 14.94 million) developing revolutionary CO2-neutral glass melting **[<457,019dc4cb-bfdc-7bfe-940f-3f63e0555127>]**, and co-developed the 'Glasy' recycling technology achieving '99.9999% purity' glass recovery **[<456,019dc4cb-bfdb-7156-a1ec-0e9dde5cc2b0>]**. Stoelzle's CEO states 'Operational excellence paves the way for future growth and innovation. elements.name: Shared Services & Synergies
elements.aiAnswer: CAG Holding provides identifiable shared services and synergies across its subsidiaries, though documentation is limited due to the holding's deliberately low public profile. The holding operates a centralized Compliance Unit: 'Neuman Aluminium has engaged the services of the Compliance Unit of our parent company, CAG Holding GmbH, to review this issue independently of Neuman Aluminium Group management' **[<481,019dc4cb-ea38-77d1-9b8f-16c1c904073d>]**. Stoelzle similarly states: 'Stoelzle has engaged the services of the Compliance Unit of our parent company, CAG Holding GmbH, to review this issue independently of Stoelzle Group management' **[<487,019dc4cb-ea3e-76b1-8840-dbeb56739a27>]**. Stoelzle explicitly acknowledges holding-level synergies: 'The firm integration within the CAG-Holding creates key synergies with Stoelzle's partner companies. Within the CAG-Holding all affiliated companies offer bespoke solutions and all-round competence in processing a whole series of modern materials' **[<484,019dc4cb-ea3b-725f-9d9a-58f192eac0e6>]**. Cross-subsidiary talent mobility is evidenced by Leopold Werdich's transfer from TUBEX Managing Director to 'a senior management position at CAG Holding GmbH from June 2024' **[<472,019dc4cb-e9e4-743b-b41a-de1e690f82a2>]**. Neuman and Stoelzle share talent development programs: students receiving Neuman scholarships 'are also given the opportunity to complete an internship at Neuman or with our colleagues at Stoelzle Oberglas GmbH' **[<490,019dc4cb-ea41-7d56-aaf0-5424a988b1fd>]**. The FORUM ALUMINIUM conference is co-organized by 'NEUMAN Aluminium in Kooperation mit PREFA Aluminiumprodukte' under CAG Holding sponsorship **[<489,019dc4cb-ea40-7afe-9684-159e0bc3e5e4>]**. Material synergies exist between aluminium-focused subsidiaries (Neuman, PREFA, TUBEX) sharing aluminium processing expertise. However, the holding 'verzichtet sogar darauf, eine eigene Website zu betreiben' (does not even maintain its own website) **[<433,019dc4cb-c636-7d31-b317-78a26b2d2656>]** and no documentation on shared services cost allocation, synergy capture metrics, or centralized procurement was found.
elements.evidenceQuote: Stoelzle regards itself as well-equipped for both the present and the future. The firm integration within the CAG-Holding (located in Niederösterreich, Austria) creates key synergies with Stoelzle's partner companies. Within the CAG-Holding all affiliated companies offer bespoke solutions and all-round competence in processing a whole series of modern materials. **[<484,019dc4cb-ea3b-725f-9d9a-58f192eac0e6>]**
elements.scoreRationale: Evidence of shared services exists but is limited. CAG Holding provides a centralized Compliance Unit that serves both Neuman Aluminium and Stoelzle for whistleblowing and compliance review **[<481,019dc4cb-ea38-77d1-9b8f-16c1c904073d>, <487,019dc4cb-ea3e-76b1-8840-dbeb56739a27>]**. Leopold Werdich's transfer from TUBEX to a senior management position at CAG Holding in June 2024 suggests growing holding-level management functions **[<472,019dc4cb-e9e4-743b-b41a-de1e690f82a2>]**. Stoelzle explicitly states that 'firm integration within the CAG-Holding creates key synergies with Stoelzle's partner companies' **[<484,019dc4cb-ea3b-725f-9d9a-58f192eac0e6>]**. Cross-subsidiary collaboration is evidenced by the FORUM ALUMINIUM conference co-organized by Neuman and PREFA **[<489,019dc4cb-ea40-7afe-9684-159e0bc3e5e4>]** and shared scholarship programs between Neuman and Stoelzle **[<490,019dc4cb-ea41-7d56-aaf0-5424a988b1fd>]**. However, the holding operates with extreme discretion — no website, no public reporting — making it impossible to assess the full scope of shared services, cost allocation, or synergy capture metrics.
elements.dataGap: No documentation on shared services cost allocation, synergy capture metrics, centralized procurement savings, shared IT infrastructure, or holding-level overhead cost structure. The holding's deliberate opacity prevents assessment of unrealized synergy potential.
sourcesUsed: Web Search — Neuman People and Career **[<490,019dc4cb-ea41-7d56-aaf0-5424a988b1fd>]**
Web Search — CAG Holding trend article **[<433,019dc4cb-c636-7d31-b317-78a26b2d2656>]**

strengths: Deep domain expertise across aluminium and glass value chains with 200+ years of glass heritage (Stoelzle) and 80+ years in aluminium roofing (PREFA), supported by 9,800 employees across 40+ production sites globally **[<435,019dc4cb-c638-797a-9630-42a686cb0492>, <484,019dc4cb-ea3b-725f-9d9a-58f192eac0e6>, <441,019dc4cb-b780-76d2-bd3b-71f1d3077765>]**

Strong innovation culture evidenced by PREFA solar roof tile, Neuman's structured open innovation management system with university partnerships, Stoelzle's ZeroCO2Glas project (EUR 14.94M), and TUBEX's multiple packaging awards **[<468,019dc4cb-b97c-711d-9c0f-0cfd36786caa>, <457,019dc4cb-bfdc-7bfe-940f-3f63e0555127>, <444,019dc4cb-b783-723b-861d-a5849e1f8bfd>, <473,019dc4cb-e9e5-7145-918a-6f0065230eb5>]**

Vertically integrated aluminium processing capabilities spanning foundry, extrusion, impact extrusion, and profile processing across Neuman's four business units, with automotive-grade ISO/TS 16949 quality standards **[<461,019dc4cb-b975-706d-8ecc-bc84c2e4a97b>, <420,019dc4cb-8f31-7c94-b0ce-ab74022f8773>]**

Sustainability leadership with Stoelzle achieving EcoVadis Gold Medal (top 2% of glass manufacturers), SBTi-approved decarbonization targets, and PREFA using 77% recycled aluminium with 100% renewable electricity since 2020 **[<456,019dc4cb-bfdb-7156-a1ec-0e9dde5cc2b0>, <459,019dc4cb-bfde-7fe5-87a6-4f6ff6462161>, <486,019dc4cb-ea3d-7be5-963a-1a67ec6b7403>]**

Centralized compliance function at CAG Holding level serving multiple subsidiaries, with cross-subsidiary talent mobility and shared scholarship programs **[<481,019dc4cb-ea38-77d1-9b8f-16c1c904073d>, <487,019dc4cb-ea3e-76b1-8840-dbeb56739a27>, <490,019dc4cb-ea41-7d56-aaf0-5424a988b1fd>]**
weaknesses: Extreme opacity at holding level — CAG Holding does not maintain a website, does not publish consolidated financial reports, and operates with minimal public disclosure, making strategic assessment and stakeholder communication difficult **[<433,019dc4cb-c636-7d31-b317-78a26b2d2656>]**

No documented consolidated digital transformation strategy, group-wide ERP system, or data analytics/AI capabilities at the holding level despite significant subsidiary-level technology investments **[<433,019dc4cb-c636-7d31-b317-78a26b2d2656>]**
Absence of publicly available consolidated operational KPIs, cost-to-revenue ratios, productivity metrics, or lean manufacturing program documentation at the holding level
Limited evidence of formalized shared services beyond compliance — no documented centralized procurement, shared IT infrastructure, or financial shared services center
opportunities: Leverage cross-subsidiary aluminium expertise (Neuman, PREFA, TUBEX) to create integrated material science R&D center and shared procurement for aluminium raw materials, potentially reducing input costs across the group

Capitalize on growing demand for sustainable building materials and electric vehicle components — PREFA's solar roof tiles and Neuman's EV battery components (BMW i3 battery pressure plates since 2013) position the group well for green transition markets **[<469,019dc4cb-b97d-795a-8cf7-58feb42ffb76>, <444,019dc4cb-b783-723b-861d-a5849e1f8bfd>]**
Expand digital capabilities at holding level to enable group-wide data analytics, predictive maintenance, and operational benchmarking across 40+ production sites

Stoelzle's glass electrification leadership and ZeroCO2Glas project could establish first-mover advantage in carbon-neutral glass manufacturing, commanding premium pricing in sustainability-conscious markets **[<457,019dc4cb-bfdc-7bfe-940f-3f63e0555127>, <459,019dc4cb-bfde-7fe5-87a6-4f6ff6462161>]**
threats: Energy price volatility and supply disruption risk — both glass manufacturing and aluminium processing are highly energy-intensive, creating significant exposure to European energy market instability

Automotive industry cyclicality and EV transition uncertainty affecting Neuman Aluminium's automotive division, which serves OEMs like BMW with components that may face design changes in next-generation vehicles **[<469,019dc4cb-b97d-795a-8cf7-58feb42ffb76>]**

Competition from alternative materials (plastics, composites, carbon fiber) threatening aluminium's market share in automotive lightweight construction and packaging applications **[<480,019dc4cb-e9ec-714a-a0dc-ae27187f29ee>]**

Succession risk — the group is wholly owned by Dr. Cornelius Alexander Grupp with generational transition underway (son Cornelius Grupp appointed TUBEX CEO in 2023, son August Grupp appointed Stoelzle CEO), creating potential strategic continuity risk **[<474,019dc4cb-e9e6-750e-b03b-8aad3ff74b0f>, <416,019dc4cb-8f2d-779a-be93-4734cee0f372>]**

leadership: [Shared Services & Synergies] — The Compliance Unit at CAG Holding serves both Neuman Aluminium and Stoelzle for whistleblowing review **[<481,019dc4cb-ea38-77d1-9b8f-16c1c904073d>, <487,019dc4cb-ea3e-76b1-8840-dbeb56739a27>]**, but no other centralized shared services are documented — what additional holding-level functions (procurement, IT, finance, HR) exist, and what is the annual cost of the holding overhead relative to group revenue of EUR 1.56 billion?

elements.name: Organizational Structure
elements.aiAnswer: Cultural Assets Group is headquartered in Riyadh with strategic offices in AlUla, Jeddah, London, Paris, and Unaizah **[<422,019dc4d6-e2de-73ca-8f4f-695ad610bc7c>, <434,019dc4d6-dcfe-7982-91c5-3be424fecc71>]**. The holding consolidates seven leading companies and over twenty innovative brands under a unified platform **[<422,019dc4d6-e2de-73ca-8f4f-695ad610bc7c>, <473,019dc4d7-2b8f-7e06-851f-d727e01e3fa8>]**. The seven subsidiary companies are: Backyard Symphony, Knowliom, Knowliom Museum Studio, Sign, Haal, Operal, and Backyard Immersions **[<422,019dc4d6-e2de-73ca-8f4f-695ad610bc7c>, <434,019dc4d6-dcfe-7982-91c5-3be424fecc71>]**. The leadership structure includes Chairman Abdullah Khalid Al Zamil **[<444,019dc4d7-04e5-7bd0-adf7-48647cbc5fb4>, <446,019dc4d7-04e7-7c87-9e0a-bb320b4b3276>]** and CEO Abdulaziz AlSulaim **[<473,019dc4d7-2b8f-7e06-851f-d727e01e3fa8>, <476,019dc4d7-2b92-7469-b863-f239d0449e01>]**. The group has also established a joint venture, Knowliom-CMS, with Chargeurs Museum Studio and Zamil Trade and Services **[<460,019dc4d7-0e54-7773-9160-494e498a9231>, <467,019dc4d7-2fe1-7314-9e0e-b71a11af1f57>]**. The group collaborates with national stakeholders including the Ministry of Culture, Royal Commission for AlUla, Diriyah Gate Development Authority, ROSHN, and Mohammed Bin Salman Foundation (Misk) **[<473,019dc4d7-2b8f-7e06-851f-d727e01e3fa8>, <478,019dc4d7-2b94-7281-9d1c-d3b536b501ad>]**. However, no internal organizational chart, reporting lines, spans of control, or number of organizational layers were found in any documents. The structure appears to be a classic holding company model with subsidiary autonomy, but the degree of centralization vs. decentralization, shared services model, and governance framework between the holding and subsidiaries remain undocumented. The recent launch (May 2025) suggests the organizational structure is still being formalized. The multi-geography presence across five cities and two continents adds structural complexity that requires clear governance frameworks.
elements.evidenceQuote: Headquartered in Riyadh, with strategic offices in AlUla, Jeddah, London, Paris, and Unaizah, the group consolidates seven leading companies and over twenty innovative brands, including Backyard Symphony, Knowliom, Knowliom Museum Studio, Sign, Haal, Operal and Backyard Immersions, under a unified platform, to accelerate the development of private sector enterprises operating in the cultural domain.
elements.scoreRationale: Score of 3 reflects an adequate but unproven structure. The holding model with seven subsidiaries and multi-geography presence demonstrates strategic intent **[<422,019dc4d6-e2de-73ca-8f4f-695ad610bc7c>, <434,019dc4d6-dcfe-7982-91c5-3be424fecc71>]**, and the appointment of a Chairman and CEO provides basic governance **[<444,019dc4d7-04e5-7bd0-adf7-48647cbc5fb4>, <473,019dc4d7-2b8f-7e06-851f-d727e01e3fa8>]**. However, the organization was only formally launched in May 2025, meaning the structure is nascent. No documentation exists on spans of control, organizational layers, shared services, or governance frameworks between holding and subsidiaries. The score cannot be higher without evidence of structural effectiveness, agility mechanisms, or clear reporting hierarchies.

elements.name: Talent & Skills
elements.aiAnswer: Cultural Assets Group has a dedicated workforce of over 250 specialized professionals **[<431,019dc4d6-dcfb-76a9-8375-8dc7d2ed5f89>, <433,019dc4d6-dcfd-738e-bb08-e97592f2ba06>, <434,019dc4d6-dcfe-7982-91c5-3be424fecc71>]**. The group boasts comprehensive expertise across multiple disciplines including museum design and construction, destination development, cultural events and exhibitions, experience design, community engagement, activation programs, interactive visual production, marketing and communications, and cultural retail **[<431,019dc4d6-dcfb-76a9-8375-8dc7d2ed5f89>, <433,019dc4d6-dcfd-738e-bb08-e97592f2ba06>]**. elements.name: Culture & Values
elements.aiAnswer: Cultural Assets Group's stated values center on authenticity, excellence, cultural enrichment, and sustainability **[<417,019dc4d6-aef7-703d-a850-f5f0bcab6825>, <433,019dc4d6-dcfd-738e-bb08-e97592f2ba06>]**. CEO Abdulaziz AlSulaim described the group as 'a unified, purpose-driven platform committed to advancing the Kingdom's cultural priorities' **[<473,019dc4d7-2b8f-7e06-851f-d727e01e3fa8>]**. The group's website states it is 'committed to building an inspiring and sustainable cultural narrative with an impact that transcends time and deepens community connections' **[<417,019dc4d6-aef7-703d-a850-f5f0bcab6825>]**. One subsidiary, Knowliom, is certified as a Great Place to Work **[<459,019dc4d7-0e53-755c-b50e-588dbafcd134>]**, which suggests strong cultural foundations in at least one part of the group. Knowliom was 'founded with a dream to inspire the next generation to become science and culture champions' **[<459,019dc4d7-0e53-755c-b50e-588dbafcd134>]**. Backyard Symphony describes fostering 'a culture of creativity and innovation' **[<457,019dc4d7-0e51-7339-a2f3-8adf4e3dbbfa>, <458,019dc4d7-0e52-7493-914a-0f6b2130bb1b>]**. However, no group-wide cultural assessment, values framework, cultural integration plan for the seven merging companies, or culture measurement tools were found. The consolidation of seven previously independent companies with potentially different cultures, work practices, and values systems represents a significant cultural integration challenge. Research on Saudi organizational culture indicates that 'Saudi Organizations with collaborative, transparent cultures, and strong employee recognition programs had 37% lower turnover rates' **[<482,019dc4d7-45cc-7eab-a476-ca1748d89eb1>]**, underscoring the importance of deliberate cultural design in the Saudi context.

elements.name: Change Readiness
elements.aiAnswer: Cultural Assets Group's formation itself represents a major organizational transformation — consolidating seven independent companies and twenty brands into a single holding platform **[<421,019dc4d6-e2dd-7d60-8d03-4e3a047c6627>, <422,019dc4d6-e2de-73ca-8f4f-695ad610bc7c>, <473,019dc4d7-2b8f-7e06-851f-d727e01e3fa8>]**. The group has also announced strategic acquisitions (The Stage, The Pop Up, Beyond) and a SAR 850 million investment fund **[<471,019dc4d7-2b8d-7bdf-9dfd-cfd9ba8bb7aa>, <475,019dc4d7-2b91-7e17-9446-b5212f440c5e>, <476,019dc4d7-2b92-7469-b863-f239d0449e01>]**, indicating an aggressive growth and transformation agenda. The group was 'formed in direct alignment with Saudi Vision 2030 and the Kingdom's broader cultural renaissance' **[<422,019dc4d6-e2de-73ca-8f4f-695ad610bc7c>, <477,019dc4d7-2b93-788b-b57d-8e75e0651048>]**, demonstrating strategic change orientation. The establishment of the Knowliom-CMS joint venture with Chargeurs Museum Studio **[<460,019dc4d7-0e54-7773-9160-494e498a9231>, <467,019dc4d7-2fe1-7314-9e0e-b71a11af1f57>]** shows capability in cross-border partnership formation. However, no change management methodology, transformation roadmap, integration management office (IMO) structure, or change readiness assessment was found. The simultaneous challenges of: (1) integrating seven companies under a new holding, (2) executing new acquisitions, (3) launching an SAR 850 million investment fund, and (4) establishing international operations across five cities and two continents represent an extraordinarily complex change agenda for a newly formed organization with 250 employees. No evidence exists of formal change management capability, change leadership training, or organizational agility mechanisms. The absence of documented change management infrastructure for such a complex transformation agenda is a significant risk.
elements.evidenceQuote: This strategic formation is in direct response to Saudi Vision 2030, which clearly articulated ambitious goals for the cultural creative economy, establishing robust government initiatives that laid the groundwork for substantial private sector investment. Cultural Assets Group leverages this momentum, becoming a critical engine and a catalyst for sector growth, investment attraction, and innovation, aligning seamlessly with the Kingdom's vision for cultural and economic transformation.
elements.scoreRationale: Score of 2 reflects change challenges given the scale of transformation underway without documented change management infrastructure. While the group demonstrates strategic ambition and has successfully launched as a consolidated entity **[<421,019dc4d6-e2dd-7d60-8d03-4e3a047c6627>, <473,019dc4d7-2b8f-7e06-851f-d727e01e3fa8>]**, the simultaneous execution of company integration, new acquisitions **[<471,019dc4d7-2b8d-7bdf-9dfd-cfd9ba8bb7aa>, <475,019dc4d7-2b91-7e17-9446-b5212f440c5e>]**, international expansion, and fund launch without documented change management methodology, IMO structure, or change readiness assessment represents significant risk. The organization is only weeks old (launched May 2025), and no track record of successful transformation exists at the group level. The score reflects the gap between transformation ambition and documented change management capability.

strengths.text: Portfolio diversification with evidence of cross-subsidiary collaboration: the subsidiaries cited operate in adjacent value chains and explicitly reference internal synergies as a source of advantage, indicating some parenting value already exists even without a fully formalized group model [0-320, 0-338].

Strong subsidiary-level operational depth: the pack shows long heritage, specialized industrial know-how, and significant scale across 9,800 employees and 40+ production sites, suggesting that core assets are real and capable even if the holding layer is opaque [0-435, 0-484, 0-441].

Credible innovation and sustainability capabilities at subsidiary level, including SBTi-approved targets, EcoVadis Gold recognition, renewable electricity usage, recycled input content, and funded decarbonization projects, which can support differentiation and future value creation [0-456, 0-459, 0-486, 0-457].

Long-term ownership orientation appears to support strategic continuity and patient capital, which can be advantageous in cyclical, asset-heavy sectors and in pursuing transformation programs [0-333, 0-339, 0-340].

weaknesses.text: Material data-integrity gap: the pillar pack appears to mix two incompatible entity profiles (an Austrian industrial family holding and a Saudi cultural platform), so the evidence base is not fully reconcilable at entity level. This is the most important limitation and makes any assessment provisional.

The holding-level strategic core is underdeveloped: no formal mission, vision, public strategy, parenting purpose, strategic cascade, or group-wide KPI framework is evidenced, so coherence exists more by implication than by design [0-333].

Extreme opacity at the center: no holding website, no consolidated public reporting, and no visible group-level operational KPI set, digital strategy, market intelligence system, or quantified synergy model were found, weakening stakeholder confidence and management control [0-433].

Governance and organization appear incomplete for a multi-entity group: no documented delegation of authority, succession planning, executive evaluation framework, leadership pipeline, or clear holding-subsidiary operating model were evidenced.

Customer and market analytics are weakly evidenced: no TAM/SAM/SOM, market share, customer concentration, NPS/CSAT, or formal competitive analysis were found, suggesting the center may be under-instrumented for portfolio steering.

Material assessment blind spot: P7 Risk & Resilience and P8 Growth & Strategic Options are unscored and empty, leaving major gaps in the enterprise view of downside protection and future strategic pathways.

opportunities.text: Build a real corporate center: formalize group purpose, portfolio thesis, KPI cascade, capital-allocation rules, shared services, and quantified synergy targets to convert a collection of strong assets into a value-adding holding structure.

Create group-wide data, digital, and risk infrastructure across the portfolio, enabling benchmarking, predictive maintenance, procurement leverage, and faster management intervention across multiple sites and subsidiaries.

Use subsidiary-level ESG and innovation credentials as the basis for a stronger external equity story, premium positioning, and targeted M&A or vertical-integration moves in sustainability-linked segments [0-373, 0-457, 0-459].
Clarify the entity perimeter and reporting boundary, then complete the missing P7/P8 workstreams; doing so would materially improve strategic optionality, financing readiness, and stakeholder trust.

threats.text: Strategic drift is the primary enterprise threat: without a clear holding identity, strategic cascade, and accountability framework, subsidiaries can optimize locally while the portfolio underperforms collectively.

Leadership continuity and oversight risk are insufficiently managed: the evidence shows single-owner dependency in one profile and executive/board overlap in another, while no succession framework is documented in either case [0-333].

Transparency and reporting expectations are rising; the current privacy/opacity posture may become increasingly costly as lenders, regulators, customers, and ESG stakeholders demand clearer governance and performance evidence [0-333].
Integration and culture risk is elevated because the group appears to be managing multiple subsidiaries and acquisitions without an evidenced change-management or cultural-integration model.

Capital allocation risk is meaningful where evidence points to rising holding overhead, negative free cash flow, liquidity pressure, or constrained access to public capital; without stronger center discipline, growth could dilute value rather than compound it.

strategicHypothesis.aiDraft:
Cultural Assets Group appears to have a classic holding-company challenge: the underlying assets look materially stronger than the corporate center. Across the pillar pack, the most credible positive signal is not a polished group strategy but the existence of capable subsidiaries with real operating depth, innovation activity, sustainability credentials, and some evidence of cross-company collaboration. In other words, there are building blocks for a strong parent, but the parent advantage itself is not yet clearly evidenced.

The central strategic issue is therefore not whether the subsidiaries are good assets; it is whether the holding can systematically create more value than those businesses would create on a stand-alone basis. Today, the answer appears only partially. The pack points to missing or weak holding-level fundamentals: no clearly articulated mission or parenting purpose, no visible strategic cascade, no group KPI architecture, limited public transparency, weak documented market intelligence, and insufficient evidence of governance instruments such as delegation of authority, succession planning, and executive accountability. That combination creates a high risk that the group remains a portfolio owner rather than a portfolio multiplier.

A major caution is required: the evidence base is internally inconsistent. Some pillars describe an Austrian industrial, family-owned portfolio in aluminium, glass, and biomass; others describe a Saudi cultural platform with SAR-denominated financials, government alignment, and different subsidiaries. In addition, P7 and P8 are empty. As a result, any entity-level conclusion must be treated as provisional until management validates the legal perimeter, reporting boundary, and source pack integrity.

Given that limitation, the best strategic hypothesis is this: if CAG clarifies its perimeter and then professionalizes the center, it has a realistic path to a step-change in value creation. The highest-priority moves would be to define the corporate thesis, codify the operating model between center and subsidiaries, install consolidated reporting and risk management, quantify synergy opportunities, and communicate a coherent external narrative. If those actions are taken, the group could translate subsidiary quality into a defendable holding premium. If they are not, the likely outcome is continued strategic ambiguity, governance friction, weak stakeholder confidence, and under-realized portfolio value.

KEY ORGANIZATIONAL OBSERVATIONS

Span of Control: Group CEO has 12 direct reports (6 GEC + 6 Subsidiary CEOs) — at the upper limit of effective span. Consider adding a Group Deputy CEO or COO with subsidiary oversight responsibility.

Saudization: Group-wide Saudization rate is 72% (target: 80% by 2026). Highest in Sub 4 (Arts Education, 85%) and lowest in Sub 3 (Digital Content, 55% — tech talent scarcity).

Gender Diversity: 34% female across group; 43% at GEC level (3 of 7); 33% at Subsidiary CEO level (2 of 6). Board: 22% female (2 of 9).

Average Tenure: GEC average tenure is 3.0 years (relatively new team). Subsidiary CEO average tenure is 3.5 years. Longest-serving: Dr. Mona Al-Turki (Sub 4, 5 years). Shortest: Yara Al-Amri (Group CMO, 1 year).

Holding Company Overhead: 120 FTE at SAR 42M cost represents 2.0% of group revenue. Benchmark for strategic holding companies is 1.5–2.5% — CAG is within range but should monitor as revenue scales.

Reporting Matrix: Subsidiary functional heads (Finance, HR) have a solid line to their Subsidiary CEO and a dotted line to the corresponding Group function head. Document Title: Cultural Assets Group — Corporate Strategy Plan 2024–2028 Classification: Confidential — Board Approved Version: 3.2 Final Date: January 15, 2024 Prepared by: Office of the Group CEO & Group Strategy DivisionApproved by: CAG Board of Directors — Resolution #BD-2024-003 (January 12, 2024) Format: PDF (48 pages)



TABLE OF CONTENTS

Chairman's Foreword

Group CEO's Strategic Letter

Who We Are — Mission, Vision & Values

Our Theory of Value Creation (Parenting Purpose)

Strategic Context & Environmental Scan

Group Strategic Pillars 2024–2028

Portfolio Strategy & Subsidiary Mandates

Financial Ambition & Capital Allocation Framework

Governance of Strategy Execution

Key Risks to Strategy

Appendices



1. CHAIRMAN'S FOREWORD

The Cultural Assets Group stands at an inflection point. Over the past decade, we have assembled a portfolio of six distinctive subsidiaries operating across the cultural economy — spanning heritage tourism, live entertainment, digital content, arts education, cultural real estate development, and creative services. Each subsidiary was acquired or incubated because of its intrinsic connection to culture as an asset class.

As I reflect on our journey, I am proud of what we have built but clear-eyed about what lies ahead. The global cultural economy is projected to reach USD 8.2 trillion by 2028 (UNESCO/Oxford Economics, 2023). Yet this growth will not be evenly distributed. It will accrue to organizations that can operate at the intersection of authenticity, technology, and scale — precisely where CAG is positioned.

This strategy document represents the Board's consensus on where we are headed and how we will get there. It is the product of six months of deliberation, subsidiary consultations, external advisory input, and rigorous financial modeling.

Sheikh Ahmed Al-Farsi Chairman, CAG Board of Directors



2. GROUP CEO'S STRATEGIC LETTER

To our Board, leadership teams, and stakeholders:

Our first strategic cycle (2019–2023) was defined by portfolio assembly. We acquired four subsidiaries, incubated two, and established the holding company's central functions. We achieved consolidated revenue of SAR 2.1 billion in FY2023, up from SAR 680 million in FY2019 — a CAGR of 32.6%.

Our second strategic cycle (2024–2028) must be defined by portfolio optimization and value multiplication. We must shift from "collection" to "connection" — unlocking the synergies between our subsidiaries that justified their acquisition in the first place.

Three convictions underpin this strategy:

Culture is the new infrastructure. Governments and consumers are investing in cultural experiences at unprecedented rates. Our subsidiaries sit on irreplaceable cultural assets.

The holding company must earn its right to exist. Every central function, every governance mechanism, every capital allocation decision must demonstrably add value that subsidiaries could not create alone.

Digital is not a pillar — it is the atmosphere. Every subsidiary strategy must be digitally native. We will invest SAR 400 million over five years in digital transformation across the group.

Nora Al-Rashid Group CEO, Cultural Assets Group



3. WHO WE ARE — MISSION, VISION & VALUES

3.1 Mission Statement

"To preserve, activate, and scale cultural assets for the enrichment of communities and the creation of sustainable economic value."

3.2 Vision Statement

"By 2028, CAG will be the Middle East and North Africa's leading cultural economy group — recognized for the authenticity of our cultural offerings, the excellence of our operations, and the impact of our investments on communities and stakeholders."

3.3 Core Values

Value

Definition

Behavioral Anchor

Authenticity

We honor the integrity of cultural assets and never compromise heritage for short-term gain

Every product/experience must pass the "Cultural Integrity Review"

Excellence

We pursue operational and creative excellence in everything we do

Zero tolerance for mediocrity; continuous improvement embedded in KPIs

Stewardship

We are custodians, not owners, of cultural assets — we hold them in trust for future generations

Long-term value creation over short-term extraction

Collaboration

We believe the group is greater than the sum of its parts

Cross-subsidiary projects are rewarded; silos are actively dismantled

Courage

We take bold, calculated bets on the future of culture

Innovation budget ring-fenced; failure-tolerant experimentation encouraged

3.4 Strategic Identity Summary

CAG is a strategic holding company (not a financial holding or passive investor). We actively shape subsidiary strategies, allocate capital with conviction, provide shared services where scale advantages exist, and intervene when subsidiaries underperform. Our parenting style is best described as "Strategic Architect" — we set the blueprint, resource the build, and monitor progress, but we empower subsidiary CEOs to lead execution.



4. OUR THEORY OF VALUE CREATION (PARENTING PURPOSE)

4.1 The Parenting Advantage Framework

CAG creates value for its subsidiaries through five mechanisms:

#

Value Creation Mechanism

Description

Example

1

Capital Allocation

Centralized capital allocation enables investment in highest-return opportunities across the portfolio, rather than each subsidiary self-funding

SAR 120M redirected from Subsidiary 4 (mature, cash-generative) to Subsidiary 2 (high-growth, capital-hungry) in 2023

2

Talent & Leadership Development

Group-wide talent pool, leadership rotation program, and centralized executive recruitment

Group CHRO manages top-50 leadership pipeline; 3 subsidiary CEOs rotated in 2022–2023

3

Shared Services & Scale Economies

Centralized procurement, finance, legal, IT infrastructure, and marketing analytics

Group procurement saved SAR 45M in FY2023 through consolidated vendor contracts

4

Brand & Reputation Halo

The CAG brand provides credibility, government access, and partnership leverage that individual subsidiaries could not achieve alone

CAG brand enabled Subsidiary 1 to secure a 25-year government concession valued at SAR 800M

5

Strategic Synergy Orchestration

Active identification and execution of cross-subsidiary revenue and cost synergies

"Cultural Passport" product (cross-selling across Subsidiaries 1, 2, and 5) generated SAR 28M incremental revenue in FY2023

4.2 Corporate-Level Strategy

CAG's corporate-level strategy is a Related-Linked Diversification strategy. Our subsidiaries are linked by:

A common focus on cultural assets as the core resource

Shared customer segments (cultural tourists, experience seekers, government/institutional buyers)

Complementary capabilities (content creation, venue management, digital distribution, education)

Geographic overlap (primarily MENA, with selective international expansion)

We explicitly reject unrelated diversification. Any future acquisition or incubation must pass the "Cultural Nexus Test": Does this entity's core business fundamentally depend on, or contribute to, the cultural economy?



5. STRATEGIC CONTEXT & ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN

5.1 Macro-Environmental Analysis (PESTEL)

Factor

Key Trends

Implication for CAG

Time Horizon

Political

Saudi Vision 2030 allocating SAR 50B+ to culture & entertainment; UAE cultural investment accelerating; Egypt cultural heritage monetization

Massive tailwind; government as customer, partner, and regulator simultaneously

2024–2030

Economic

MENA GDP growth 3.2% (IMF 2024); tourism recovery post-COVID at 112% of 2019 levels; inflation moderating to 2.8%

Favorable demand environment; cost pressures easing

2024–2026

Social

Youth demographic bulge (65% under 35 in KSA); rising demand for experiential consumption; cultural identity as social currency

Core demand driver; product design must be youth-centric and Instagram-worthy

Document Title: Cultural Assets Group — Corporate Strategy Plan 2024–2028 Classification: Confidential — Board Approved Version: 3.2 Final Date: January 15, 2024 Prepared by: Office of the Group CEO & Group Strategy DivisionApproved by: CAG Board of Directors — Resolution #BD-2024-003 (January 12, 2024) Format: PDF (48 pages)



TABLE OF CONTENTS

Chairman's Foreword

Group CEO's Strategic Letter

Who We Are — Mission, Vision & Values

Our Theory of Value Creation (Parenting Purpose)

Strategic Context & Environmental Scan

Group Strategic Pillars 2024–2028

Portfolio Strategy & Subsidiary Mandates

Financial Ambition & Capital Allocation Framework

Governance of Strategy Execution

Key Risks to Strategy

Appendices



1. CHAIRMAN'S FOREWORD

The Cultural Assets Group stands at an inflection point. Over the past decade, we have assembled a portfolio of six distinctive subsidiaries operating across the cultural economy — spanning heritage tourism, live entertainment, digital content, arts education, cultural real estate development, and creative services. Each subsidiary was acquired or incubated because of its intrinsic connection to culture as an asset class.

As I reflect on our journey, I am proud of what we have built but clear-eyed about what lies ahead. The global cultural economy is projected to reach USD 8.2 trillion by 2028 (UNESCO/Oxford Economics, 2023). Yet this growth will not be evenly distributed. It will accrue to organizations that can operate at the intersection of authenticity, technology, and scale — precisely where CAG is positioned.

This strategy document represents the Board's consensus on where we are headed and how we will get there. It is the product of six months of deliberation, subsidiary consultations, external advisory input, and rigorous financial modeling.

Sheikh Ahmed Al-Farsi Chairman, CAG Board of Directors



2. GROUP CEO'S STRATEGIC LETTER

To our Board, leadership teams, and stakeholders:

Our first strategic cycle (2019–2023) was defined by portfolio assembly. We acquired four subsidiaries, incubated two, and established the holding company's central functions. We achieved consolidated revenue of SAR 2.1 billion in FY2023, up from SAR 680 million in FY2019 — a CAGR of 32.6%.

Our second strategic cycle (2024–2028) must be defined by portfolio optimization and value multiplication. We must shift from "collection" to "connection" — unlocking the synergies between our subsidiaries that justified their acquisition in the first place.

Three convictions underpin this strategy:

Culture is the new infrastructure. Governments and consumers are investing in cultural experiences at unprecedented rates. Our subsidiaries sit on irreplaceable cultural assets.

The holding company must earn its right to exist. Every central function, every governance mechanism, every capital allocation decision must demonstrably add value that subsidiaries could not create alone.

Digital is not a pillar — it is the atmosphere. Every subsidiary strategy must be digitally native. We will invest SAR 400 million over five years in digital transformation across the group.

Nora Al-Rashid Group CEO, Cultural Assets Group



3. WHO WE ARE — MISSION, VISION & VALUES

3.1 Mission Statement

"To preserve, activate, and scale cultural assets for the enrichment of communities and the creation of sustainable economic value."

3.2 Vision Statement

"By 2028, CAG will be the Middle East and North Africa's leading cultural economy group — recognized for the authenticity of our cultural offerings, the excellence of our operations, and the impact of our investments on communities and stakeholders."

3.3 Core Values

Value

Definition

Behavioral Anchor

Authenticity

We honor the integrity of cultural assets and never compromise heritage for short-term gain

Every product/experience must pass the "Cultural Integrity Review"

Excellence

We pursue operational and creative excellence in everything we do

Zero tolerance for mediocrity; continuous improvement embedded in KPIs

Stewardship

We are custodians, not owners, of cultural assets — we hold them in trust for future generations

Long-term value creation over short-term extraction

Collaboration

We believe the group is greater than the sum of its parts

Cross-subsidiary projects are rewarded; silos are actively dismantled

Courage

We take bold, calculated bets on the future of culture

Innovation budget ring-fenced; failure-tolerant experimentation encouraged

3.4 Strategic Identity Summary

CAG is a strategic holding company (not a financial holding or passive investor). We actively shape subsidiary strategies, allocate capital with conviction, provide shared services where scale advantages exist, and intervene when subsidiaries underperform. Our parenting style is best described as "Strategic Architect" — we set the blueprint, resource the build, and monitor progress, but we empower subsidiary CEOs to lead execution.



4. OUR THEORY OF VALUE CREATION (PARENTING PURPOSE)

4.1 The Parenting Advantage Framework

CAG creates value for its subsidiaries through five mechanisms:

#

Value Creation Mechanism

Description

Example

1

Capital Allocation

Centralized capital allocation enables investment in highest-return opportunities across the portfolio, rather than each subsidiary self-funding

SAR 120M redirected from Subsidiary 4 (mature, cash-generative) to Subsidiary 2 (high-growth, capital-hungry) in 2023

2

Talent & Leadership Development

Group-wide talent pool, leadership rotation program, and centralized executive recruitment

Group CHRO manages top-50 leadership pipeline; 3 subsidiary CEOs rotated in 2022–2023

3

Shared Services & Scale Economies

Centralized procurement, finance, legal, IT infrastructure, and marketing analytics

Group procurement saved SAR 45M in FY2023 through consolidated vendor contracts

4

Brand & Reputation Halo

The CAG brand provides credibility, government access, and partnership leverage that individual subsidiaries could not achieve alone

CAG brand enabled Subsidiary 1 to secure a 25-year government concession valued at SAR 800M

5

Strategic Synergy Orchestration

Active identification and execution of cross-subsidiary revenue and cost synergies

"Cultural Passport" product (cross-selling across Subsidiaries 1, 2, and 5) generated SAR 28M incremental revenue in FY2023

4.2 Corporate-Level Strategy

CAG's corporate-level strategy is a Related-Linked Diversification strategy. Our subsidiaries are linked by:

A common focus on cultural assets as the core resource

Shared customer segments (cultural tourists, experience seekers, government/institutional buyers)

Complementary capabilities (content creation, venue management, digital distribution, education)

Geographic overlap (primarily MENA, with selective international expansion)

We explicitly reject unrelated diversification. Any future acquisition or incubation must pass the "Cultural Nexus Test": Does this entity's core business fundamentally depend on, or contribute to, the cultural economy?

Document Title: Cultural Assets Group — Corporate Strategy Plan 2024–2028 Classification: Confidential — Board Approved Version: 3.2 Final Date: January 15, 2024 Prepared by: Office of the Group CEO & Group Strategy DivisionApproved by: CAG Board of Directors — Resolution #BD-2024-003 (January 12, 2024) Format: PDF (48 pages)



TABLE OF CONTENTS

Chairman's Foreword

Group CEO's Strategic Letter

Who We Are — Mission, Vision & Values

Our Theory of Value Creation (Parenting Purpose)

Strategic Context & Environmental Scan

Group Strategic Pillars 2024–2028

Portfolio Strategy & Subsidiary Mandates

Financial Ambition & Capital Allocation Framework

Governance of Strategy Execution

Key Risks to Strategy

Appendices



1. CHAIRMAN'S FOREWORD

The Cultural Assets Group stands at an inflection point. Over the past decade, we have assembled a portfolio of six distinctive subsidiaries operating across the cultural economy — spanning heritage tourism, live entertainment, digital content, arts education, cultural real estate development, and creative services. Each subsidiary was acquired or incubated because of its intrinsic connection to culture as an asset class.

As I reflect on our journey, I am proud of what we have built but clear-eyed about what lies ahead. The global cultural economy is projected to reach USD 8.2 trillion by 2028 (UNESCO/Oxford Economics, 2023). Yet this growth will not be evenly distributed. It will accrue to organizations that can operate at the intersection of authenticity, technology, and scale — precisely where CAG is positioned.

This strategy document represents the Board's consensus on where we are headed and how we will get there. It is the product of six months of deliberation, subsidiary consultations, external advisory input, and rigorous financial modeling.

Sheikh Ahmed Al-Farsi Chairman, CAG Board of Directors



2. GROUP CEO'S STRATEGIC LETTER

To our Board, leadership teams, and stakeholders:

Our first strategic cycle (2019–2023) was defined by portfolio assembly. We acquired four subsidiaries, incubated two, and established the holding company's central functions. We achieved consolidated revenue of SAR 2.1 billion in FY2023, up from SAR 680 million in FY2019 — a CAGR of 32.6%.

Our second strategic cycle (2024–2028) must be defined by portfolio optimization and value multiplication. We must shift from "collection" to "connection" — unlocking the synergies between our subsidiaries that justified their acquisition in the first place.

Three convictions underpin this strategy:

Culture is the new infrastructure. Governments and consumers are investing in cultural experiences at unprecedented rates. Our subsidiaries sit on irreplaceable cultural assets.

The holding company must earn its right to exist. Every central function, every governance mechanism, every capital allocation decision must demonstrably add value that subsidiaries could not create alone.

Digital is not a pillar — it is the atmosphere. Every subsidiary strategy must be digitally native. We will invest SAR 400 million over five years in digital transformation across the group.

Nora Al-Rashid Group CEO, Cultural Assets Group



3. WHO WE ARE — MISSION, VISION & VALUES

3.1 Mission Statement

"To preserve, activate, and scale cultural assets for the enrichment of communities and the creation of sustainable economic value."

3.2 Vision Statement

"By 2028, CAG will be the Middle East and North Africa's leading cultural economy group — recognized for the authenticity of our cultural offerings, the excellence of our operations, and the impact of our investments on communities and stakeholders."

3.3 Core Values

Value

Definition

Behavioral Anchor

Authenticity

We honor the integrity of cultural assets and never compromise heritage for short-term gain

Every product/experience must pass the "Cultural Integrity Review"

Excellence

We pursue operational and creative excellence in everything we do

Zero tolerance for mediocrity; continuous improvement embedded in KPIs

Stewardship

We are custodians, not owners, of cultural assets — we hold them in trust for future generations

Long-term value creation over short-term extraction

Collaboration

We believe the group is greater than the sum of its parts

Cross-subsidiary projects are rewarded; silos are actively dismantled

Courage

We take bold, calculated bets on the future of culture

Innovation budget ring-fenced; failure-tolerant experimentation encouraged

3.4 Strategic Identity Summary

CAG is a strategic holding company (not a financial holding or passive investor). We actively shape subsidiary strategies, allocate capital with conviction, provide shared services where scale advantages exist, and intervene when subsidiaries underperform. Our parenting style is best described as "Strategic Architect" — we set the blueprint, resource the build, and monitor progress, but we empower subsidiary CEOs to lead execution.



4. OUR THEORY OF VALUE CREATION (PARENTING PURPOSE)

4.1 The Parenting Advantage Framework

CAG creates value for its subsidiaries through five mechanisms:

#

Value Creation Mechanism

Description

Example

1

Capital Allocation

Centralized capital allocation enables investment in highest-return opportunities across the portfolio, rather than each subsidiary self-funding

SAR 120M redirected from Subsidiary 4 (mature, cash-generative) to Subsidiary 2 (high-growth, capital-hungry) in 2023

2

Talent & Leadership Development

Group-wide talent pool, leadership rotation program, and centralized executive recruitment

Group CHRO manages top-50 leadership pipeline; 3 subsidiary CEOs rotated in 2022–2023

3

Shared Services & Scale Economies

Centralized procurement, finance, legal, IT infrastructure, and marketing analytics

Group procurement saved SAR 45M in FY2023 through consolidated vendor contracts

4

Brand & Reputation Halo

The CAG brand provides credibility, government access, and partnership leverage that individual subsidiaries could not achieve alone

CAG brand enabled Subsidiary 1 to secure a 25-year government concession valued at SAR 800M

5

Strategic Synergy Orchestration

Active identification and execution of cross-subsidiary revenue and cost synergies

"Cultural Passport" product (cross-selling across Subsidiaries 1, 2, and 5) generated SAR 28M incremental revenue in FY2023

4.2 Corporate-Level Strategy

CAG's corporate-level strategy is a Related-Linked Diversification strategy. Our subsidiaries are linked by:

A common focus on cultural assets as the core resource

Shared customer segments (cultural tourists, experience seekers, government/institutional buyers)

Complementary capabilities (content creation, venue management, digital distribution, education)

Geographic overlap (primarily MENA, with selective international expansion)

We explicitly reject unrelated diversification. Any future acquisition or incubation must pass the "Cultural Nexus Test": Does this entity's core business fundamentally depend on, or contribute to, the cultural economy?



5. STRATEGIC CONTEXT & ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN

5.2 Industry Analysis — Cultural Economy Value Chain

The cultural economy value chain consists of four layers:

Cultural Asset Origination — Heritage sites, artistic creation, IP development

Cultural Asset Activation — Experiences, events, exhibitions, education

Cultural Asset Distribution — Digital platforms, media, licensing, merchandising

Cultural Asset Monetization — Ticketing, sponsorship, real estate, government contracts

CAG's portfolio spans all four layers, which is a distinctive competitive advantage. Most competitors operate in one or two layers.

5.4 SWOT Summary (Pre-Assessment — CEO's Perspective)



Positive

Negative

Internal

Strengths: Unique portfolio spanning full cultural value chain; strong government relationships; SAR 2.1B revenue base; talented subsidiary CEOs

Weaknesses: Synergies underexploited; digital maturity uneven across subsidiaries; holding company overhead questioned by some board members; financial reporting not yet fully consolidated in real-time

External

Opportunities: Vision 2030 cultural investment wave; digital/AI transformation of cultural experiences; international expansion (Egypt, Morocco, Turkey); "Cultural Passport" product scaling

Threats: Government entities competing directly; talent war for creative/tech professionals; regulatory uncertainty in new markets; economic downturn reducing discretionary cultural spending

KEY ORGANIZATIONAL OBSERVATIONS

Span of Control: Group CEO has 12 direct reports (6 GEC + 6 Subsidiary CEOs) — at the upper limit of effective span. Consider adding a Group Deputy CEO or COO with subsidiary oversight responsibility.

Saudization: Group-wide Saudization rate is 72% (target: 80% by 2026). Highest in Sub 4 (Arts Education, 85%) and lowest in Sub 3 (Digital Content, 55% — tech talent scarcity).

Gender Diversity: 34% female across group; 43% at GEC level (3 of 7); 33% at Subsidiary CEO level (2 of 6). Board: 22% female (2 of 9).

Average Tenure: GEC average tenure is 3.0 years (relatively new team). Subsidiary CEO average tenure is 3.5 years. Longest-serving: Dr. Mona Al-Turki (Sub 4, 5 years). Shortest: Yara Al-Amri (Group CMO, 1 year).

P1.name: Strategic Identity & Vision
P1.description: What is the entity's reason for being and where is it headed?

execSummary.aiDraft:
• Cultural Assets Group (CAG) has a publicly stated vision and mission on its website, but both are aspirational and lack specificity, measurability, or time-bound targets — the vision speaks of 'crafting a narrative that resonates across generations' and the mission of 'building a powerful economic ecosystem' without defining success metrics **[<81,019dc6ac-3737-7daf-9353-79a8c0fd13b5>, <91,019dc6ac-3267-71a6-a6be-eeea07999a68>]**
• Strategic intent is anchored to Saudi Vision 2030 and the $47.9 billion cultural sector GDP target, but CAG has not articulated its own specific share of that market, revenue targets, or SMART objectives beyond the SAR 850 million Osoul Fund **[<14,019dc6ab-bcb1-79be-be48-601b5953c757>, <45,019dc6ab-fb65-760e-a4ca-a5b2fa746943>]**
• The value proposition is emerging — CAG positions itself as the Kingdom's largest privately-owned cultural enterprise bridging 'creativity and capital,' but differentiation from government cultural entities (Ministry of Culture, Cultural Development Fund) and potential private competitors remains unclear **[<41,019dc6ab-fb61-7402-9480-140fc3fc42be>, <59,019dc6ab-fa91-7ed2-852b-68aabea567d1>]**
• Strategic coherence is partially evidenced through the Osoul Fund, acquisitions (The Stage, Beyond, The Pop Up), and partnerships (Al Madinah Region Development Authority, IN4 Group), but no formal strategy document, balanced scorecard, or cascaded strategic plan has been identified **[<61,019dc6ac-16a9-72fb-9565-6318ac159290>, <94,019dc6ac-326a-75ba-bdc5-60f34b0898a0>]**
• Parenting purpose is implicitly defined through consolidation of seven companies and twenty brands under a unified platform, but the specific value-add mechanisms (shared services, capital allocation model, synergy realization, governance framework) are not documented in publicly available sources **[<14,019dc6ab-bcb1-79be-be48-601b5953c757>, <85,019dc6ac-373b-7bce-aa09-d97af896525a>]**

P2.name: Governance & Leadership
P2.description: How is the entity governed and led?

execSummary.aiDraft:
• Cultural Assets Group is a newly launched (May 2025) privately-owned holding entity uniting seven companies and 20+ brands across Saudi Arabia's cultural and creative industries, with a board of at least six members including a mix of executive and non-executive directors **[<41,019dc6b8-e81d-78b4-96b1-968a20810483>, <61,019dc6b9-051b-7066-b5ff-b3c20efd6623>]**
• The board is chaired by Abdullah Khaled AlZamel (also CEO of Raz Capital), with Group CEO Abdulaziz AlSulaim, COO Amr AlMojadedi, and CCO Bassam AlRefi serving as executive board members, alongside two identified non-executive members (Muhammad Ali Akhter and Yasser Abdulaziz AlSanie) **[<41,019dc6b8-e81d-78b4-96b1-968a20810483>, <61,019dc6b9-051b-7066-b5ff-b3c20efd6623>]**
• No publicly available evidence was found of formal board committees (audit, risk, nomination, remuneration), delegation of authority frameworks, KPI cascading mechanisms, or succession planning — critical governance infrastructure gaps for a holding entity managing seven subsidiaries and an SAR 850 million investment fund **[<23,019dc6b8-c92a-7442-b252-0ea21619c7af>, <111,019dc6b9-47fa-7caa-af57-9dea3b8843b2>]**
• The leadership team demonstrates relevant sector expertise — the CEO has over a decade in cultural strategy, the CFO (Qasim Zureigat) brings 20+ years including IFRS and governance expertise, and the COO has 18+ years spanning cultural infrastructure and financial services **[<22,019dc6b8-c929-7ef3-87ce-8dea84c03204>, <32,019dc6b8-cec9-70d9-a4ea-dbba74b2a499>]**
• As a newly formed entity (2025), the group's governance maturity is at an early stage; while strategic alignment with Vision 2030 and high-profile government stakeholder relationships are strong, the absence of documented governance frameworks, performance management systems, and a clear parenting style definition represents significant risk for a holding managing complex multi-subsidiary operations **[<21,019dc6b8-c928-737a-9a86-388f4dab45ba>, <94,019dc6b9-2674-7e20-9765-c6095157278f>]**

elements.name: Board Composition & Effectiveness
elements.aiAnswer:
• The board comprises at least six identified members: Chairman Abdullah Khaled AlZamel; two non-executive members (Muhammad Ali Akhter and Yasser Abdulaziz AlSanie); and three executive members who are also C-suite officers — Group CEO Abdulaziz Musaed AlSulaim, COO Amr Nadeem AlMojadedi, and CCO Bassam Murad AlRefi **[<41,019dc6b8-e81d-78b4-96b1-968a20810483>, <61,019dc6b9-051b-7066-b5ff-b3c20efd6623>]**
• The board has a majority of executive members (3 executive vs. 2 identified non-executive), which raises concerns about independence and the board's ability to provide objective oversight and challenge to management **[<41,019dc6b8-e81d-78b4-96b1-968a20810483>]**
• One board member (unnamed in full but referenced on the Cultural Assets website) is noted for expertise in board governance, IFRS, internal control systems, financial reporting quality, and risk management and compliance frameworks **[<19,019dc6b8-ac71-769e-b83c-02c78520b357>, <51,019dc6b8-e65f-7b84-a025-f4595d513bbe>]**
• No evidence was found of formal board committees (audit, risk, nomination, remuneration), board meeting cadence, board evaluation processes, or a skills matrix — all of which are standard governance infrastructure for a holding entity of this scale **[<41,019dc6b8-e81d-78b4-96b1-968a20810483>]**
• The Chairman (AlZamel) is also CEO of Raz Capital and co-founder of Raz Group (managing 150+ companies), suggesting significant external commitments that may affect time availability for board duties **[<19,019dc6b8-ac71-769e-b83c-02c78520b357>, <57,019dc6b8-e665-7e3f-93c0-caba86a036d3>]**
elements.evidenceQuote: Abdullah Khaled AlZamel · Chairman of the Board of Directors · Muhammad Ali Akhter · Board Member (Non-Executive) · Yasser Abdulaziz AlSanie · Board Member (Non-Executive) · Abdulaziz Musaed Alsulaim · Board Member, and Group CEO (Executive) · Amr Nadeem AlMojadedi · Board Member and Chief Operating Officer (Executive) · Bassam Murad AlRefi · Board Member, and Chief Creative Officer (Executive)
elements.sourceDocument: Cultural Assets Group official website — Board of Directors page **[<41,019dc6b8-e81d-78b4-96b1-968a20810483>, <61,019dc6b9-051b-7066-b5ff-b3c20efd6623>]**
elements.scoreRationale: The board exists with a defined composition of executive and non-executive members, but the majority-executive composition raises independence concerns. No evidence of board committees, meeting cadence, skills matrix, board evaluation, or formal governance charter was found in any publicly available source, which is a significant gap for a holding entity managing seven subsidiaries and an SAR 850 million investment fund **[<41,019dc6b8-e81d-78b4-96b1-968a20810483>, <61,019dc6b9-051b-7066-b5ff-b3c20efd6623>, <23,019dc6b8-c92a-7442-b252-0ea21619c7af>]**.
elements.dataGap: Board committee structure (audit, risk, nomination, remuneration), board meeting frequency and attendance records, board skills matrix, independence criteria applied, board evaluation process, and whether any independent directors exist beyond the two non-executive members

elements.aiAnswer:
• Group CEO Abdulaziz AlSulaim is described as a 'cultural strategist and creative economy leader with over a decade of experience in shaping institutions and initiatives that bridge heritage, innovation, and entrepreneurship' **[<32,019dc6b8-cec9-70d9-a4ea-dbba74b2a499>, <48,019dc6b8-e824-7eba-8638-b9d395f0dfb9>]**
• CFO Qasim Mohammad Zureigat brings over 20 years of experience including roles as CFO of Naqi Water Company (Saudi listed), academic positions in accounting, and consulting for governmental and private entities; he is noted for expertise in IFRS, governance, and internal control systems **[<22,019dc6b8-c929-7ef3-87ce-8dea84c03204>]**
• COO Amr AlMojadedi has 18+ years spanning cultural infrastructure, experiential design, financial services, and engineering, with prior leadership roles at Saudi National Bank in affluent banking, corporate banking governance, and retail banking expansion **[<22,019dc6b8-c929-7ef3-87ce-8dea84c03204>]**
• CCO Bassam AlRefi serves as Board Member and Chief Creative Officer, though limited public information is available on his specific background **[<61,019dc6b9-051b-7066-b5ff-b3c20efd6623>, <81,019dc6b9-2c42-7143-89dc-75b0771543c1>]**
• Mohammed Zakaria Khoujah is identified as a board member with experience at Backyard Symphony in entertainment and event management **[<61,019dc6b9-051b-7066-b5ff-b3c20efd6623>, <84,019dc6b9-2c45-7429-bbc1-c9db9f86b745>]**
• No evidence of formal succession planning, leadership development programs, or bench strength assessment was found in any publicly available source

elements.name: Decision-Making Architecture
elements.aiAnswer:
• No publicly available documentation was found describing the group's delegation of authority framework, decision rights matrix, or escalation protocols between the holding and its seven subsidiaries **[<41,019dc6b8-e81d-78b4-96b1-968a20810483>, <61,019dc6b9-051b-7066-b5ff-b3c20efd6623>]**
• The group's stated role includes 'coordinating the planning and execution of giga cultural projects with high efficiency, ensuring alignment across the Group's subsidiaries' and 'acquiring local companies to achieve the desired integration across the Group's subsidiaries,' suggesting centralized strategic decision-making at the holding level **[<25,019dc6b8-c92c-7f24-b5de-afb39075c09b>, <33,019dc6b8-ceca-73dc-93d0-b2433d76dcf1>]**
• The CEO's dual role as board member and Group CEO, combined with the COO and CCO also sitting on the board, suggests a concentrated decision-making structure where executive management and board oversight overlap significantly **[<41,019dc6b8-e81d-78b4-96b1-968a20810483>, <61,019dc6b9-051b-7066-b5ff-b3c20efd6623>]**
• Saudi corporate governance context is relevant: research notes that Saudi companies tend toward centralized decision-making where 'approvals need to be obtained from the top of the organisation' and 'delegation of authority often requires chair or board approval of transactions that could be delegated to management committees' **[<94,019dc6b9-2674-7e20-9765-c6095157278f>]**
• The group operates across multiple geographies (Riyadh, AlUla, Jeddah, London, Paris, Unaizah) with 250+ professionals, which requires a robust delegation framework that is not evidenced **[<70,019dc6b9-0524-7314-8209-f1030467343c>, <92,019dc6b9-2672-73ca-b7d5-8df6b358796c>]**
elements.evidenceQuote: Coordinating the planning and execution of giga cultural projects with high efficiency, ensuring alignment across the Group's subsidiaries.
elements.sourceDocument: Cultural Assets Group About page **[<25,019dc6b8-c92c-7f24-b5de-afb39075c09b>, <33,019dc6b8-ceca-73dc-93d0-b2433d76dcf1>]**
elements.scoreRationale: While the group articulates a coordinating role for giga-projects and subsidiary alignment, no formal delegation of authority framework, decision rights matrix, or escalation protocols were found in any publicly available source. The overlap of executive management and board membership (3 of 6 board members are C-suite executives) raises concerns about separation of oversight and execution **[<41,019dc6b8-e81d-78b4-96b1-968a20810483>, <94,019dc6b9-2674-7e20-9765-c6095157278f>]**. For a holding entity with seven subsidiaries across six locations, this represents a significant governance gap.
elements.dataGap: Delegation of authority matrix, decision rights framework between holding and subsidiaries, escalation protocols, investment approval thresholds, and documentation of which decisions are reserved for the board vs. delegated to management or subsidiary boards

elements.aiAnswer:
• No publicly available evidence was found of KPI frameworks, performance management systems, consequence management mechanisms, or accountability structures at either the holding or subsidiary level
• The group's mission references outcomes such as 'elevate the economic value of cultural and creative industries' and 'leave a lasting impact by designing programs and subsidiaries that build legacies,' but these are aspirational statements without documented measurable targets or accountability mechanisms **[<23,019dc6b8-c92a-7442-b252-0ea21619c7af>, <35,019dc6b8-cecc-7b20-99b0-66634fc64063>]**
• The launch of the SAR 850 million Osoul Private Investment Fund with Cultural Development Fund financing suggests external accountability to government stakeholders, but the specific governance and reporting requirements of this fund are not publicly documented **[<23,019dc6b8-c92a-7442-b252-0ea21619c7af>, <111,019dc6b9-47fa-7caa-af57-9dea3b8843b2>]**
• The group collaborates with major national stakeholders (Ministry of Culture, Royal Commission for AlUla, Diriyah Gate Development Authority, ROSHN, Misk), which likely imposes project-level accountability requirements, though these are not publicly detailed **[<24,019dc6b8-c92b-7065-93b2-b9e0228e11fa>, <92,019dc6b9-2672-73ca-b7d5-8df6b358796c>]**
• No annual report, governance report, or performance disclosure was found for the group, which is consistent with its status as a privately-held entity but limits external accountability assessment
