elements.scoreRationale: No evidence of formal KPI frameworks, performance management systems, board-level performance dashboards, consequence management, or accountability structures was found in any publicly available source. While the group's collaboration with government entities likely imposes some project-level accountability, the absence of any documented performance management architecture at the holding level represents a critical gap for an entity managing seven subsidiaries and a major investment fund **[<23,019dc6b8-c92a-7442-b252-0ea21619c7af>, <111,019dc6b9-47fa-7caa-af57-9dea3b8843b2>]**.
elements.dataGap: KPI framework and cascading methodology from board to subsidiaries, performance management system documentation, board performance dashboards, consequence management policies, annual performance reporting, and accountability mechanisms for subsidiary CEOs

elements.name: Parenting Style
elements.aiAnswer:
• The group positions itself as a strategic guide and active operator, describing its role as 'a strategic catalyst for investment, consolidation, and sector innovation' that manages 'a portfolio of cultural enterprises and intellectual properties' **[<21,019dc6b8-c928-737a-9a86-388f4dab45ba>, <23,019dc6b8-c92a-7442-b252-0ea21619c7af>]**
• The holding's stated functions include acquiring companies, coordinating giga-project execution, providing sponsorship opportunities, launching community initiatives, and developing training programs — suggesting deep operational involvement beyond pure financial holding **[<33,019dc6b8-ceca-73dc-93d0-b2433d76dcf1>]**
• The group unites seven companies (Backyard Symphony, Knowliom, Knowliom Museum Studio, Sign, Haal, Operal, Backyard Immersions) and 20+ brands under a 'single, integrated platform,' with recent acquisitions of The Stage, Beyond, and The Pop Up announced in October 2025 **[<35,019dc6b8-cecc-7b20-99b0-66634fc64063>, <70,019dc6b9-0524-7314-8209-f1030467343c>, <111,019dc6b9-47fa-7caa-af57-9dea3b8843b2>]**
• The CEO's statement that 'we exist to grow the sector, back ambitious ideas, and support the scale and sustainability of cultural enterprises' suggests a strategic guide orientation, while the operational coordination of giga-projects suggests active operator tendencies **[<35,019dc6b8-cecc-7b20-99b0-66634fc64063>, <25,019dc6b8-c92c-7f24-b5de-afb39075c09b>]**
• No evidence was found of differentiated parenting approaches for subsidiaries at different maturity levels, or a formal parenting advantage framework
elements.evidenceQuote: Cultural Assets Group is the largest privately-owned cultural and creative group in Saudi Arabia, dedicated to shaping the Kingdom's cultural future through strategic investment, innovation, and ecosystem development. As an institutional leader, the Group builds and manages a portfolio of cultural enterprises and intellectual properties operating across a wide spectrum of the cultural and creative industry.
elements.sourceDocument: Cultural Assets Group press releases and website **[<23,019dc6b8-c92a-7442-b252-0ea21619c7af>, <33,019dc6b8-ceca-73dc-93d0-b2433d76dcf1>, <70,019dc6b9-0524-7314-8209-f1030467343c>]**
elements.scoreRationale: The group articulates a hybrid parenting style combining strategic guidance with active operational coordination, which is appropriate for a newly formed holding consolidating diverse cultural enterprises. However, no formal parenting advantage framework, differentiated subsidiary governance model, or documented value-creation logic for each subsidiary was found **[<23,019dc6b8-c92a-7442-b252-0ea21619c7af>, <33,019dc6b8-ceca-73dc-93d0-b2433d76dcf1>]**. The rapid acquisition pace (three acquisitions announced at a single conference in October 2025) without publicly documented integration governance raises concerns about parenting capacity **[<111,019dc6b9-47fa-7caa-af57-9dea3b8843b2>]**.
elements.dataGap: Formal parenting advantage framework, subsidiary governance model documentation, differentiated parenting approach by subsidiary maturity, integration governance for recent acquisitions, and value-creation logic articulated for each of the seven (now ten) subsidiaries

strengths: Board includes members with relevant cross-sector expertise including governance, IFRS, financial services, cultural infrastructure, and creative industries, providing a diverse skills base for a cultural holding entity **[<19,019dc6b8-ac71-769e-b83c-02c78520b357>, <22,019dc6b8-c929-7ef3-87ce-8dea84c03204>, <32,019dc6b8-cec9-70d9-a4ea-dbba74b2a499>]**

Strong strategic alignment with Saudi Vision 2030 and direct collaboration with major national stakeholders (Ministry of Culture, Royal Commission for AlUla, Diriyah Gate Development Authority, ROSHN, Misk), providing institutional legitimacy and access to flagship projects **[<24,019dc6b8-c92b-7065-93b2-b9e0228e11fa>, <92,019dc6b9-2672-73ca-b7d5-8df6b358796c>]**

Leadership team combines cultural sector depth (CEO with 10+ years in cultural strategy) with corporate rigor (CFO with 20+ years including listed company experience and academic governance credentials) **[<22,019dc6b8-c929-7ef3-87ce-8dea84c03204>, <32,019dc6b8-cec9-70d9-a4ea-dbba74b2a499>]**

Significant scale as Saudi Arabia's largest privately-owned cultural enterprise with 250+ professionals, seven subsidiaries, 20+ brands, and offices across six locations including international presence in London and Paris **[<70,019dc6b9-0524-7314-8209-f1030467343c>]**
weaknesses: Board composition is majority-executive (3 executive vs. 2 non-executive out of 6 identified members), with CEO, COO, and CCO all serving as board members, creating significant overlap between management and oversight functions **[<41,019dc6b8-e81d-78b4-96b1-968a20810483>, <61,019dc6b9-051b-7066-b5ff-b3c20efd6623>]**

No evidence of formal board committees (audit, risk, nomination, remuneration), delegation of authority frameworks, or governance charter — critical infrastructure gaps for a holding entity managing multiple subsidiaries and a major investment fund **[<41,019dc6b8-e81d-78b4-96b1-968a20810483>]**

No documented KPI framework, performance management system, succession planning, or accountability mechanisms found in any publicly available source, suggesting governance infrastructure has not kept pace with the group's rapid growth and acquisition activity **[<23,019dc6b8-c92a-7442-b252-0ea21619c7af>, <111,019dc6b9-47fa-7caa-af57-9dea3b8843b2>]**

As a newly launched entity (May 2025), governance maturity is inherently limited; the group has announced three acquisitions within months of launch without publicly documented integration governance **[<111,019dc6b9-47fa-7caa-af57-9dea3b8843b2>, <35,019dc6b8-cecc-7b20-99b0-66634fc64063>]**
opportunities: The group's early-stage status provides an opportunity to design governance infrastructure from scratch using best-in-class frameworks, avoiding legacy governance debt that established holding entities often face **[<21,019dc6b8-c928-737a-9a86-388f4dab45ba>]**

The SAR 850 million Osoul Private Investment Fund with Cultural Development Fund financing creates a natural catalyst for formalizing governance, as fund governance requirements will likely mandate audit, risk, and compliance structures **[<23,019dc6b8-c92a-7442-b252-0ea21619c7af>, <111,019dc6b9-47fa-7caa-af57-9dea3b8843b2>]**

Saudi Arabia's evolving corporate governance landscape, with increasing emphasis on governance effectiveness beyond compliance, positions the group to become a governance benchmark in the cultural sector **[<4,019dc6b8-b1c9-7d17-82ba-234b813c05d1>]**

• The Knowliom-CMS joint venture with Chargeurs Museum Studio (a global player) suggests at least one subsidiary has international partnership validation **[<82,019dc6cd-504f-7d95-a0ef-8b0567bf116e>]**

strengths: Largest privately-owned cultural enterprise in Saudi Arabia with a diversified portfolio of seven companies and 20+ brands spanning immersive experiences, museum services, creative production, and cultural lifestyle — providing sector-leading scale in a nascent market **[<41,019dc6cd-2e3c-7294-89a4-79692c798bae>, <42,019dc6cd-2e3d-774b-a0ea-bf4262464809>]**

Strong government alignment and institutional backing — collaborates with Ministry of Culture, Royal Commission for AlUla, Diriyah Gate Development Authority, ROSHN, and Misk Foundation; secured SAR 200 million CDF financing for the Osoul Fund under patronage of the Minister of Culture **[<32,019dc6cd-2797-799c-b51c-5e5c27733cd9>, <42,019dc6cd-2e3d-774b-a0ea-bf4262464809>, <84,019dc6cd-5051-79e3-8f48-3df344ada40a>]**

International presence with offices in London and Paris alongside Saudi offices in Riyadh, AlUla, Jeddah, and Unaizah, plus the Knowliom-CMS joint venture with France's Chargeurs Museum Studio **[<41,019dc6cd-2e3c-7294-89a4-79692c798bae>, <82,019dc6cd-504f-7d95-a0ef-8b0567bf116e>]**

Active acquisition strategy with three strategic acquisitions (Beyond, The Pop Up, The Stage) announced in October 2025, demonstrating consolidation capability in a fragmented cultural sector **[<71,019dc6cd-4f35-7770-8dd7-ed09faf2d2bf>, <81,019dc6cd-504e-7c6b-bb6d-97fe7b8be90b>]**
weaknesses: Zero publicly available financial data — no revenue, profitability, balance sheet, cash flow, or return metrics disclosed for the holding group or any subsidiary, making financial health assessment impossible **[<8,019dc6cd-06d0-7609-855e-c50c4a37d8ba>, <41,019dc6cd-2e3c-7294-89a4-79692c798bae>]**

Potential heavy reliance on government-linked contracts and CDF financing, creating concentration risk if government cultural spending priorities shift
No evidence of self-sustaining revenue generation or profitability — the entity appears to be in a capital deployment phase funded by external capital rather than operating cash flows
opportunities: Saudi cultural and creative industries are expected to contribute approximately $47.9 billion to GDP by 2030, with the cultural sector targeting 3% of GDP ($33 billion) — representing a massive addressable market for the group **[<35,019dc6cd-279a-7f4b-9c94-b5052738938b>, <42,019dc6cd-2e3d-774b-a0ea-bf4262464809>]**

The Osoul Private Investment Fund (SAR 850 million) positions the group as a cultural sector investment platform, potentially generating management fees and carried interest alongside operational revenue **[<32,019dc6cd-2797-799c-b51c-5e5c27733cd9>, <90,019dc6cd-5057-7cf3-8c74-abb30e4ef336>]**
threats: The Saudi cultural sector is nascent and unproven as a commercially sustainable private-sector market — the sector's growth is heavily dependent on continued government spending and Vision 2030 commitment **[<22,019dc6cd-00d0-7ddd-b2b2-0b0efbf8323d>, <23,019dc6cd-00d1-794a-957a-28ecb4897ba5>]**

Increasing competition as CDF launches multiple investment funds (SAR 375 million film fund with BSF Capital, SAR 300 million fashion fund with Merak Capital) that may compete with or fragment the cultural investment landscape **[<88,019dc6cd-5055-7bd6-96dc-ea4be4129fb5>]**

Geopolitical and macroeconomic risks — Saudi Arabia's fiscal deficit widened to SR115.63 billion in 2024, and any reduction in government cultural spending could directly impact the group's pipeline **[<91,019dc6cd-794a-7fd8-8686-b2f6ca638999>]**
Talent scarcity in the cultural and creative industries within Saudi Arabia, requiring significant investment in human capital development and potentially increasing operating costs

Document Title: Cultural Assets Group — Corporate Strategy Plan 2024–2028 Classification: Confidential — Board Approved Version: 3.2 Final Date: January 15, 2024 Prepared by: Office of the Group CEO & Group Strategy DivisionApproved by: CAG Board of Directors — Resolution #BD-2024-003 (January 12, 2024) Format: PDF (48 pages)



TABLE OF CONTENTS

Chairman's Foreword

Group CEO's Strategic Letter

Who We Are — Mission, Vision & Values

Our Theory of Value Creation (Parenting Purpose)

Strategic Context & Environmental Scan

Group Strategic Pillars 2024–2028

Portfolio Strategy & Subsidiary Mandates

Financial Ambition & Capital Allocation Framework

Governance of Strategy Execution

Key Risks to Strategy

Appendices



1. CHAIRMAN'S FOREWORD

The Cultural Assets Group stands at an inflection point. Over the past decade, we have assembled a portfolio of six distinctive subsidiaries operating across the cultural economy — spanning heritage tourism, live entertainment, digital content, arts education, cultural real estate development, and creative services. Each subsidiary was acquired or incubated because of its intrinsic connection to culture as an asset class.

As I reflect on our journey, I am proud of what we have built but clear-eyed about what lies ahead. The global cultural economy is projected to reach USD 8.2 trillion by 2028 (UNESCO/Oxford Economics, 2023). Yet this growth will not be evenly distributed. It will accrue to organizations that can operate at the intersection of authenticity, technology, and scale — precisely where CAG is positioned.

This strategy document represents the Board's consensus on where we are headed and how we will get there. It is the product of six months of deliberation, subsidiary consultations, external advisory input, and rigorous financial modeling.

Sheikh Ahmed Al-Farsi Chairman, CAG Board of Directors



2. GROUP CEO'S STRATEGIC LETTER

To our Board, leadership teams, and stakeholders:

Our first strategic cycle (2019–2023) was defined by portfolio assembly. We acquired four subsidiaries, incubated two, and established the holding company's central functions. We achieved consolidated revenue of SAR 2.1 billion in FY2023, up from SAR 680 million in FY2019 — a CAGR of 32.6%.

Our second strategic cycle (2024–2028) must be defined by portfolio optimization and value multiplication. We must shift from "collection" to "connection" — unlocking the synergies between our subsidiaries that justified their acquisition in the first place.

Three convictions underpin this strategy:

Culture is the new infrastructure. Governments and consumers are investing in cultural experiences at unprecedented rates. Our subsidiaries sit on irreplaceable cultural assets.

The holding company must earn its right to exist. Every central function, every governance mechanism, every capital allocation decision must demonstrably add value that subsidiaries could not create alone.

Digital is not a pillar — it is the atmosphere. Every subsidiary strategy must be digitally native. We will invest SAR 400 million over five years in digital transformation across the group.

Nora Al-Rashid Group CEO, Cultural Assets Group



3. WHO WE ARE — MISSION, VISION & VALUES

3.1 Mission Statement

"To preserve, activate, and scale cultural assets for the enrichment of communities and the creation of sustainable economic value."

3.2 Vision Statement

"By 2028, CAG will be the Middle East and North Africa's leading cultural economy group — recognized for the authenticity of our cultural offerings, the excellence of our operations, and the impact of our investments on communities and stakeholders."

3.3 Core Values

Value

Definition

Behavioral Anchor

Authenticity

We honor the integrity of cultural assets and never compromise heritage for short-term gain

Every product/experience must pass the "Cultural Integrity Review"

Excellence

We pursue operational and creative excellence in everything we do

Zero tolerance for mediocrity; continuous improvement embedded in KPIs

Stewardship

We are custodians, not owners, of cultural assets — we hold them in trust for future generations

Long-term value creation over short-term extraction

Collaboration

We believe the group is greater than the sum of its parts

Cross-subsidiary projects are rewarded; silos are actively dismantled

Courage

We take bold, calculated bets on the future of culture

Innovation budget ring-fenced; failure-tolerant experimentation encouraged

3.4 Strategic Identity Summary

CAG is a strategic holding company (not a financial holding or passive investor). We actively shape subsidiary strategies, allocate capital with conviction, provide shared services where scale advantages exist, and intervene when subsidiaries underperform. Our parenting style is best described as "Strategic Architect" — we set the blueprint, resource the build, and monitor progress, but we empower subsidiary CEOs to lead execution.



4. OUR THEORY OF VALUE CREATION (PARENTING PURPOSE)

4.1 The Parenting Advantage Framework

CAG creates value for its subsidiaries through five mechanisms:

#

Value Creation Mechanism

Description

Example

1

Capital Allocation

Centralized capital allocation enables investment in highest-return opportunities across the portfolio, rather than each subsidiary self-funding

SAR 120M redirected from Subsidiary 4 (mature, cash-generative) to Subsidiary 2 (high-growth, capital-hungry) in 2023

2

Talent & Leadership Development

Group-wide talent pool, leadership rotation program, and centralized executive recruitment

Group CHRO manages top-50 leadership pipeline; 3 subsidiary CEOs rotated in 2022–2023

3

Shared Services & Scale Economies

Centralized procurement, finance, legal, IT infrastructure, and marketing analytics

Group procurement saved SAR 45M in FY2023 through consolidated vendor contracts

4

Brand & Reputation Halo

The CAG brand provides credibility, government access, and partnership leverage that individual subsidiaries could not achieve alone

CAG brand enabled Subsidiary 1 to secure a 25-year government concession valued at SAR 800M

5

Strategic Synergy Orchestration

Active identification and execution of cross-subsidiary revenue and cost synergies

"Cultural Passport" product (cross-selling across Subsidiaries 1, 2, and 5) generated SAR 28M incremental revenue in FY2023

4.2 Corporate-Level Strategy

CAG's corporate-level strategy is a Related-Linked Diversification strategy. Our subsidiaries are linked by:

A common focus on cultural assets as the core resource

Shared customer segments (cultural tourists, experience seekers, government/institutional buyers)

Complementary capabilities (content creation, venue management, digital distribution, education)

Geographic overlap (primarily MENA, with selective international expansion)

We explicitly reject unrelated diversification. Any future acquisition or incubation must pass the "Cultural Nexus Test": Does this entity's core business fundamentally depend on, or contribute to, the cultural economy?



5. STRATEGIC CONTEXT & ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN

5.1 Macro-Environmental Analysis (PESTEL)

Key Trends

Implication for CAG

Time Horizon

Political

Saudi Vision 2030 allocating SAR 50B+ to culture & entertainment; UAE cultural investment accelerating; Egypt cultural heritage monetization

Massive tailwind; government as customer, partner, and regulator simultaneously

MENA GDP growth 3.2% (IMF 2024); tourism recovery post-COVID at 112% of 2019 levels; inflation moderating to 2.8%

Opportunity and threat; must invest or be disrupted

Environmental

Must integrate sustainability into operations; potential competitive differentiator

2024–2028

5.2 Industry Analysis — Cultural Economy Value Chain

The cultural economy value chain consists of four layers:

Cultural Asset Origination — Heritage sites, artistic creation, IP development

Cultural Asset Activation — Experiences, events, exhibitions, education

Cultural Asset Distribution — Digital platforms, media, licensing, merchandising

Cultural Asset Monetization — Ticketing, sponsorship, real estate, government contracts

CAG's portfolio spans all four layers, which is a distinctive competitive advantage. Most competitors operate in one or two layers.

5.4 SWOT Summary (Pre-Assessment — CEO's Perspective)



Positive

Negative

Internal

Strengths: Unique portfolio spanning full cultural value chain; strong government relationships; SAR 2.1B revenue base; talented subsidiary CEOs

Weaknesses: Synergies underexploited; digital maturity uneven across subsidiaries; holding company overhead questioned by some board members; financial reporting not yet fully consolidated in real-time

External

Opportunities: Vision 2030 cultural investment wave; digital/AI transformation of cultural experiences; international expansion (Egypt, Morocco, Turkey); "Cultural Passport" product scaling

Threats: Government entities competing directly; talent war for creative/tech professionals; regulatory uncertainty in new markets; economic downturn reducing discretionary cultural spending

KEY ORGANIZATIONAL OBSERVATIONS

Span of Control: Group CEO has 12 direct reports (6 GEC + 6 Subsidiary CEOs) — at the upper limit of effective span. Consider adding a Group Deputy CEO or COO with subsidiary oversight responsibility.

Saudization: Group-wide Saudization rate is 72% (target: 80% by 2026). Highest in Sub 4 (Arts Education, 85%) and lowest in Sub 3 (Digital Content, 55% — tech talent scarcity).

Gender Diversity: 34% female across group; 43% at GEC level (3 of 7); 33% at Subsidiary CEO level (2 of 6). Board: 22% female (2 of 9).

Average Tenure: GEC average tenure is 3.0 years (relatively new team). Subsidiary CEO average tenure is 3.5 years. Longest-serving: Dr. Mona Al-Turki (Sub 4, 5 years). Shortest: Yara Al-Amri (Group CMO, 1 year).

Holding Company Overhead: 120 FTE at SAR 42M cost represents 2.0% of group revenue. Benchmark for strategic holding companies is 1.5–2.5% — CAG is within range but should monitor as revenue scales.

Reporting Matrix: Subsidiary functional heads (Finance, HR) have a solid line to their Subsidiary CEO and a dotted line to the corresponding Group function head. This creates a matrix that enables group standards while preserving subsidiary autonomy. However, interviews suggest the dotted line is inconsistently enforced — some subsidiary Finance Directors have minimal interaction with the Group CFO.

elements.name: Mission & Vision Clarity
elements.aiAnswer:
• Mission is formally articulated in Section 3.1 of the Corporate Strategy Plan: 'To preserve, activate, and scale cultural assets for the enrichment of communities and the creation of sustainable economic value' **[<3,019dc6e3-3745-755e-ab87-a5eb2eafaa86>, <126,019dc6e3-3e26-7cee-868b-2efe750d4425>]**
• Vision is time-bound to 2028 and aspirational: 'By 2028, CAG will be the Middle East and North Africa's leading cultural economy group — recognized for the authenticity of our cultural offerings, the excellence of our operations, and the impact of our investments on communities and stakeholders' **[<5,019dc6e3-3747-79a5-a755-cd0d13ce0cf5>, <233,019dc6e3-47e8-78d2-9d6d-b304f3676538>]**
• Clear distinction exists between mission (why we exist — preserve/activate/scale cultural assets) and vision (where we are going — MENA's leading cultural economy group by 2028)
• Five core values (Authenticity, Excellence, Stewardship, Collaboration, Courage) are defined with behavioral anchors, creating an actionable values framework **[<7,019dc6e3-3749-7123-8111-af6c68b5e811>, <235,019dc6e3-47ea-7c8a-be13-1b411ec8a48b>]**
• The strategic identity is explicitly defined: 'CAG is a strategic holding company (not a financial holding or passive investor)' with a 'Strategic Architect' parenting style **[<8,019dc6e3-374a-7870-880f-22c2c3dc4976>, <121,019dc6e3-3e21-7d90-9d55-496a7dd27c85>]**
elements.evidenceQuote: To preserve, activate, and scale cultural assets for the enrichment of communities and the creation of sustainable economic value.
elements.sourceDocument: Cultural Assets Group — Corporate Strategy Plan 2024–2028
elements.scoreRationale: The mission and vision are formally documented in a Board-approved strategy plan (Resolution #BD-2024-003) **[<11,019dc6e3-374d-7029-a7ae-1a72bf654318>]**. The mission clearly articulates purpose (preserve, activate, scale cultural assets) with dual outcomes (community enrichment + economic value). The vision is time-bound (2028), geographically specific (MENA), and measurable (leading cultural economy group). Five values with behavioral anchors demonstrate operationalization. This represents best-in-class practice for a holding company.
elements.dataGap: No evidence of employee awareness surveys measuring mission/vision internalization across the 2,770 FTE workforce; no subsidiary-level mission statements found to assess alignment

elements.name: Strategic Intent
elements.aiAnswer:
• The 2024-2028 strategic cycle is explicitly defined as 'portfolio optimization and value multiplication' — a shift from the 2019-2023 cycle of 'portfolio assembly' **[<2,019dc6e3-3744-72d5-90f5-14f0cc1b6056>, <125,019dc6e3-3e25-7cf6-929f-15e3da19f39c>]**
• Five strategic pillars with quantified objectives: (A) Portfolio Synergy Acceleration — SAR 28M to SAR 200M synergy revenue; (B) Digital Transformation — Level 4/5 maturity by 2027; (C) Geographic Expansion — 3 new MENA markets contributing 15% of revenue; (D) Operational Excellence — EBITDA margin from 18.2% to 24%; (E) Talent & Culture — Top 10 Employer by 2027 **[<31,019dc6e3-3761-7489-b431-dd3df092dec4>, <40,019dc6e3-376a-7e27-9c2f-71b0e3f91d9b>, <42,019dc6e3-376c-75f9-bec7-32150558b460>, <51,019dc6e3-3775-7eae-a476-43fbeae8a2d4>, <53,019dc6e3-3777-7753-b1fa-ea231c248c96>]**
• SMART financial targets: Revenue SAR 2,100M to SAR 3,600M; EBITDA SAR 382M to SAR 864M; ROIC 9.2% to 14.5%; Net Debt/EBITDA 2.8x to 2.0x **[<86,019dc6e3-3798-7465-abb4-936e88feeb64>]**
• Capital allocation framework of SAR 1,950M over 5 years with clear governance: 61% subsidiary growth, 18% digital transformation, 17% geographic expansion, 3% innovation **[<87,019dc6e3-3799-7b63-a807-899fc45afcfa>]**
• Three strategic convictions articulated by CEO: (1) Culture is the new infrastructure; (2) The holding company must earn its right to exist; (3) Digital is not a pillar — it is the atmosphere **[<2,019dc6e3-3744-72d5-90f5-14f0cc1b6056>]**
elements.evidenceQuote: Our second strategic cycle (2024–2028) must be defined by portfolio optimization and value multiplication. We must shift from 'collection' to 'connection' — unlocking the synergies between our subsidiaries that justified their acquisition in the first place.
elements.sourceDocument: Cultural Assets Group — Corporate Strategy Plan 2024–2028
elements.scoreRationale: Strategic intent is exceptionally well-defined with SMART targets across all five pillars, each with specific initiatives, owners, timelines, and investment amounts [1-31 through 1-53]. The financial ambition is quantified at both group and subsidiary levels with FY2023 baselines and FY2028 targets **[<16,019dc6e3-3752-7825-806d-f4d0b25c9491>, <86,019dc6e3-3798-7465-abb4-936e88feeb64>]**. The capital allocation framework provides clear prioritization with governance thresholds. The CEO's three convictions provide a compelling strategic narrative. This is sector-leading practice.
elements.dataGap: No mid-cycle progress report (e.g., FY2024 actuals vs. plan) found to validate whether strategic intent is translating into execution; no evidence of initiative prioritization or sequencing trade-offs if capital becomes constrained

elements.name: Value Proposition
elements.aiAnswer:
• CAG's unique value proposition is full cultural value chain coverage across four layers: Origination, Activation, Distribution, and Monetization — 'Most competitors operate in one or two layers' **[<35,019dc6e3-3765-7194-9bd0-697527db17d5>, <36,019dc6e3-3766-7340-95e6-1b920892d98b>, <143,019dc6e3-3e37-7f1a-87e1-51ec9ba713b7>]**
• Competitive positioning is clearly mapped: #2 in MENA cultural economy by revenue (private sector); #1 in breadth of value chain coverage **[<28,019dc6e3-375e-751b-a38f-5066c1581de2>, <153,019dc6e3-3e41-7767-a832-b019cf0b64f1>]**
• Differentiation against five named competitors is articulated: vs. MBC Group (CAG has physical venues + digital), vs. Diriyah Gate (CAG is more agile and commercial), vs. Emaar Entertainment (CAG has deeper cultural authenticity), vs. Ithra (CAG has portfolio breadth vs. single-site) **[<27,019dc6e3-375d-713a-9788-b22807125aea>, <259,019dc6e3-4802-79ee-835a-60a1c668fc1e>]**
• The 'Cultural Nexus Test' provides a clear strategic filter for portfolio coherence: 'Does this entity's core business fundamentally depend on, or contribute to, the cultural economy?' **[<23,019dc6e3-3759-7719-ac72-fa49f92863b1>, <137,019dc6e3-3e31-7ba8-a8b8-f539abaa11d9>]**
• Cross-subsidiary value creation is demonstrated through the 'Cultural Passport' program generating SAR 28M in FY2023 with a target of SAR 80M by 2027 **[<31,019dc6e3-3761-7489-b431-dd3df092dec4>, <156,019dc6e3-3e44-79e0-a527-f5b24174ab17>]**
elements.evidenceQuote: CAG's portfolio spans all four layers, which is a distinctive competitive advantage. Most competitors operate in one or two layers.
elements.sourceDocument: Cultural Assets Group — Corporate Strategy Plan 2024–2028
elements.scoreRationale: The value proposition is well-differentiated with clear competitive mapping against five named competitors **[<27,019dc6e3-375d-713a-9788-b22807125aea>, <28,019dc6e3-375e-751b-a38f-5066c1581de2>]**. The four-layer value chain framework provides a compelling articulation of unique positioning. However, the value proposition is primarily internally articulated in a Board-approved strategy document — there is no evidence of external communication, customer-facing value proposition statements, or stakeholder perception data validating the claimed differentiation. The CEO's own SWOT acknowledges synergies are 'underexploited' **[<28,019dc6e3-375e-751b-a38f-5066c1581de2>]**, suggesting the full value proposition is aspirational rather than fully realized.
elements.dataGap: No customer or stakeholder perception surveys validating the value proposition; no external brand equity measurement; no evidence of how the value proposition is communicated to government partners, B2B clients, or end consumers

elements.name: Strategic Coherence
elements.aiAnswer:
• Clear cascade from vision to strategy to execution: Vision (MENA's leading cultural economy group by 2028) → 5 Strategic Pillars → 17+ named initiatives with owners, timelines, and budgets → Portfolio mandates per subsidiary (BCG classification: 3 Stars, 1 Question Mark, 2 Cash Cows) → KPI cascade at Group/Subsidiary/Initiative levels [1-5, 1-14, 1-31 through 1-53, 1-63]
• Governance architecture supports coherence: Board (quarterly), GEC (bi-weekly), Investment Committee (monthly), Subsidiary Boards (quarterly), Full Group Strategy Review (semi-annual June & December) **[<61,019dc6e3-377f-726c-8afd-6dd34180f26f>, <92,019dc6e3-379e-76a3-ad1b-0dcd042ffb35>]**
• Strategic planning calendar is formalized with monthly/quarterly rhythm from January Board approval through December pre-approval cycle **[<65,019dc6e3-3783-7445-89f4-de8dea092edd>, <170,019dc6e3-3e52-75b6-bb75-867824b74e45>]**
• However, the organizational structure document reveals a tension: 'the dotted line is inconsistently enforced — some subsidiary Finance Directors have minimal interaction with the Group CFO' **[<430,019dc6e3-38b6-77fb-99ce-f859de5680d2>]**, suggesting a gap between designed coherence and operational reality
• The CEO's SWOT acknowledges 'financial reporting not yet consolidated in real-time' and 'holding company overhead questioned by board members' **[<28,019dc6e3-375e-751b-a38f-5066c1581de2>, <153,019dc6e3-3e41-7767-a832-b019cf0b64f1>]**, indicating coherence challenges in practice
elements.evidenceQuote: CAG is a strategic holding company (not a financial holding or passive investor). We actively shape subsidiary strategies, allocate capital with conviction, provide shared services where scale advantages exist, and intervene when subsidiaries underperform. Our parenting style is best described as 'Strategic Architect' — we set the blueprint, resource the build, and monitor progress, but we empower subsidiary CEOs to lead execution.
elements.sourceDocument: Cultural Assets Group — Corporate Strategy Plan 2024–2028
elements.scoreRationale: The strategic architecture demonstrates strong coherence on paper with a clear vision-to-execution cascade, formalized governance forums, and a three-level KPI framework **[<63,019dc6e3-3781-7c5d-b271-b977b7a4629f>, <65,019dc6e3-3783-7445-89f4-de8dea092edd>]**. The BCG-inspired portfolio classification with differentiated mandates per subsidiary shows sophisticated portfolio management **[<14,019dc6e3-3750-7f8e-9858-718f61aefd2d>]**. However, two documented weaknesses reduce the score: (1) the dotted-line matrix between subsidiary functional heads and group functions is 'inconsistently enforced' **[<430,019dc6e3-38b6-77fb-99ce-f859de5680d2>]**, and (2) financial reporting is 'not yet consolidated in real-time' **[<28,019dc6e3-375e-751b-a38f-5066c1581de2>]**. These indicate that the designed coherence has not fully translated into operational reality.
elements.dataGap: No strategy execution dashboard or balanced scorecard showing actual vs. planned performance across the five pillars; no evidence of how contradictions between subsidiary autonomy and group control are resolved in practice

elements.name: Parenting Purpose
elements.aiAnswer:
• Parenting purpose is explicitly defined through a dedicated chapter (Section 4) titled 'Our Theory of Value Creation (Parenting Purpose)' with five named mechanisms: (1) Capital Allocation, (2) Talent & Leadership Development, (3) Shared Services & Scale Economies, (4) Brand & Reputation Halo, (5) Strategic Synergy Orchestration **[<9,019dc6e3-374b-7b44-9097-1cab92ea259b>, <20,019dc6e3-3756-7970-a36e-e96175131997>, <122,019dc6e3-3e22-71f3-be6e-ba79877acb60>, <134,019dc6e3-3e2e-7ee7-a3a6-bdcda923ca73>]**
• Each mechanism has concrete examples: SAR 120M capital reallocation from Sub 4 to growth subsidiaries; CEO rotation in 2022; group procurement savings; 25-year government concession enabled by CAG brand; Cultural Passport generating SAR 28M **[<20,019dc6e3-3756-7970-a36e-e96175131997>, <242,019dc6e3-47f1-7443-b7b6-9f0dafbcc5c3>]**
• Corporate-level strategy is explicitly defined as 'Related-Linked Diversification' with four linkage dimensions: common cultural asset focus, shared customer segments, complementary capabilities, and geographic overlap **[<22,019dc6e3-3758-7a7f-a2c0-0929519dc4b2>, <136,019dc6e3-3e30-7e88-95db-9301dd08583a>]**
• The 'Cultural Nexus Test' provides a clear acquisition/incubation filter rejecting unrelated diversification **[<23,019dc6e3-3759-7719-ac72-fa49f92863b1>]**
• Self-awareness is demonstrated: the CEO states 'The holding company must earn its right to exist' **[<2,019dc6e3-3744-72d5-90f5-14f0cc1b6056>]**, and the SWOT acknowledges 'holding company overhead questioned by board members' and 'synergies underexploited' **[<28,019dc6e3-375e-751b-a38f-5066c1581de2>]**
elements.evidenceQuote: CAG creates value for its subsidiaries through five mechanisms... The holding company must earn its right to exist. Every central function, every governance mechanism, every capital allocation decision must demonstrably add value that subsidiaries could not create alone.
elements.sourceDocument: Cultural Assets Group — Corporate Strategy Plan 2024–2028
elements.scoreRationale: The parenting purpose is among the most explicitly articulated elements in the strategy, with a dedicated framework, five named mechanisms, and concrete examples **[<9,019dc6e3-374b-7b44-9097-1cab92ea259b>, <20,019dc6e3-3756-7970-a36e-e96175131997>]**. The Related-Linked Diversification strategy and Cultural Nexus Test demonstrate sophisticated corporate strategy thinking **[<22,019dc6e3-3758-7a7f-a2c0-0929519dc4b2>, <23,019dc6e3-3759-7719-ac72-fa49f92863b1>]**. However, the score is capped at 4 because the CEO's own SWOT acknowledges that synergies are 'underexploited' and 'holding company overhead questioned by board members' **[<28,019dc6e3-375e-751b-a38f-5066c1581de2>]**, indicating the parenting advantage is well-designed but not yet fully proven. The holding company's 120 FTE at SAR 42M (2.0% of revenue) is within benchmark range but lacks a formal parenting value quantification **[<430,019dc6e3-38b6-77fb-99ce-f859de5680d2>]**.
elements.dataGap: No formal parenting value quantification (e.g., total value added by holding vs. total holding cost); no subsidiary CEO satisfaction survey on holding company value-add; no evidence of how the 'Strategic Architect' model is perceived by subsidiary leadership

strengths: Exceptionally well-articulated mission, vision, and strategic identity with Board-approved documentation, time-bound targets, and behavioral value anchors **[<3,019dc6e3-3745-755e-ab87-a5eb2eafaa86>, <5,019dc6e3-3747-79a5-a755-cd0d13ce0cf5>, <7,019dc6e3-3749-7123-8111-af6c68b5e811>]**

Unique full cultural value chain coverage (Origination through Monetization) across six subsidiaries — a competitive moat that no MENA competitor replicates **[<35,019dc6e3-3765-7194-9bd0-697527db17d5>, <36,019dc6e3-3766-7340-95e6-1b920892d98b>]**

Sophisticated parenting purpose framework with five explicit value creation mechanisms and concrete examples of capital reallocation and synergy orchestration **[<9,019dc6e3-374b-7b44-9097-1cab92ea259b>, <20,019dc6e3-3756-7970-a36e-e96175131997>]**

[Parenting Purpose] — The strategy identifies five value creation mechanisms **[<20,019dc6e3-3756-7970-a36e-e96175131997>]**, but is there a formal annual quantification of the total value added by the holding company versus its SAR 42M annual cost **[<430,019dc6e3-38b6-77fb-99ce-f859de5680d2>]**? If not, how do you respond to board members who question the overhead?

[Strategic Intent] — Sub 3 (Digital Content) has a -5% EBIT margin and is classified as a 'Question Mark' with a path to profitability by 2026 **[<14,019dc6e3-3750-7f8e-9858-718f61aefd2d>, <16,019dc6e3-3752-7825-806d-f4d0b25c9491>]**. What are the specific milestones that would trigger a decision to divest or shut down this subsidiary if profitability is not achieved?

[Strategic Coherence] — The Group CEO has 12 direct reports (6 GEC + 6 Subsidiary CEOs), which the organizational document flags as 'at the upper limit of effective span' **[<430,019dc6e3-38b6-77fb-99ce-f859de5680d2>]**. Has the recommendation to add a Group Deputy CEO or COO with subsidiary oversight been acted upon?
team: [Mission & Vision Clarity] — Can you recite the CAG mission statement from memory, and how does it influence your day-to-day decision-making in your subsidiary or function?

[Mission & Vision Clarity] — The strategy document defines five core values with behavioral anchors **[<7,019dc6e3-3749-7123-8111-af6c68b5e811>]**. Which value do you see most consistently practiced in your subsidiary, and which one is most aspirational or least embedded?

[Strategic Intent] — Your subsidiary has specific FY2028 revenue and EBIT margin targets **[<16,019dc6e3-3752-7825-806d-f4d0b25c9491>]**. How were these targets communicated to your team, and do your individual KPIs directly link to these subsidiary-level targets?

[Strategic Intent] — The strategy identifies five pillars (Synergy, Digital, Geographic, Operational Excellence, Talent) [1-31 through 1-53]. Which pillar has the most tangible impact on your daily operations, and which feels most disconnected from your work?

[Value Proposition] — The strategy claims CAG's competitive advantage is full value chain coverage **[<35,019dc6e3-3765-7194-9bd0-697527db17d5>]**. In your operational experience, do you actively collaborate with other subsidiaries to deliver this integrated value, or do you primarily operate independently?

[Value Proposition] — The 'Cultural Passport' program generated SAR 28M in FY2023 **[<20,019dc6e3-3756-7970-a36e-e96175131997>]**. How involved is your subsidiary in this program, and what operational challenges does cross-subsidiary selling create?

[Strategic Coherence] — Your functional head (Finance, HR) has a dotted line to the corresponding Group function **[<430,019dc6e3-38b6-77fb-99ce-f859de5680d2>]**. In practice, how often do you interact with the Group function, and does this relationship add value or create bureaucracy?

[Strategic Coherence] — The strategy planning calendar shows quarterly performance reviews and semi-annual strategy reviews **[<65,019dc6e3-3783-7445-89f4-de8dea092edd>]**. Do you experience these as meaningful strategic conversations or compliance exercises?
[Parenting Purpose] — What specific service or capability does the holding company provide that your subsidiary could not provide for itself more efficiently?

[Parenting Purpose] — The strategy states CAG's parenting style is 'Strategic Architect' — setting the blueprint but empowering subsidiary CEOs to lead execution **[<8,019dc6e3-374a-7870-880f-22c2c3dc4976>]**. In your experience, does the holding company respect subsidiary autonomy, or does it intervene too much or too little?

KEY ORGANIZATIONAL OBSERVATIONS

Span of Control: Group CEO has 12 direct reports (6 GEC + 6 Subsidiary CEOs) — at the upper limit of effective span. Consider adding a Group Deputy CEO or COO with subsidiary oversight responsibility.

Saudization: Group-wide Saudization rate is 72% (target: 80% by 2026). Highest in Sub 4 (Arts Education, 85%) and lowest in Sub 3 (Digital Content, 55% — tech talent scarcity).

Gender Diversity: 34% female across group; 43% at GEC level (3 of 7); 33% at Subsidiary CEO level (2 of 6). Board: 22% female (2 of 9).

Average Tenure: GEC average tenure is 3.0 years (relatively new team). Subsidiary CEO average tenure is 3.5 years. Longest-serving: Dr. Mona Al-Turki (Sub 4, 5 years). Shortest: Yara Al-Amri (Group CMO, 1 year).

Holding Company Overhead: 120 FTE at SAR 42M cost represents 2.0% of group revenue. Benchmark for strategic holding companies is 1.5–2.5% — CAG is within range but should monitor as revenue scales.

Reporting Matrix: Subsidiary functional heads (Finance, HR) have a solid line to their Subsidiary CEO and a dotted line to the corresponding Group function head. This creates a matrix that enables group standards while preserving subsidiary autonomy. However, interviews suggest the dotted line is inconsistently enforced — some subsidiary Finance Directors have minimal interaction with the Group CFO.

Document Title: Cultural Assets Group — Corporate Strategy Plan 2024–2028 Classification: Confidential — Board Approved Version: 3.2 Final Date: January 15, 2024 Prepared by: Office of the Group CEO & Group Strategy DivisionApproved by: CAG Board of Directors — Resolution #BD-2024-003 (January 12, 2024) Format: PDF (48 pages)



TABLE OF CONTENTS

Chairman's Foreword

Group CEO's Strategic Letter

Who We Are — Mission, Vision & Values

Our Theory of Value Creation (Parenting Purpose)

Strategic Context & Environmental Scan

Group Strategic Pillars 2024–2028

Portfolio Strategy & Subsidiary Mandates

Financial Ambition & Capital Allocation Framework

Governance of Strategy Execution

Key Risks to Strategy

Appendices



1. CHAIRMAN'S FOREWORD

The Cultural Assets Group stands at an inflection point. Over the past decade, we have assembled a portfolio of six distinctive subsidiaries operating across the cultural economy — spanning heritage tourism, live entertainment, digital content, arts education, cultural real estate development, and creative services. Each subsidiary was acquired or incubated because of its intrinsic connection to culture as an asset class.

As I reflect on our journey, I am proud of what we have built but clear-eyed about what lies ahead. The global cultural economy is projected to reach USD 8.2 trillion by 2028 (UNESCO/Oxford Economics, 2023). Yet this growth will not be evenly distributed. It will accrue to organizations that can operate at the intersection of authenticity, technology, and scale — precisely where CAG is positioned.

This strategy document represents the Board's consensus on where we are headed and how we will get there. It is the product of six months of deliberation, subsidiary consultations, external advisory input, and rigorous financial modeling.

Sheikh Ahmed Al-Farsi Chairman, CAG Board of Directors



2. GROUP CEO'S STRATEGIC LETTER

To our Board, leadership teams, and stakeholders:

Our first strategic cycle (2019–2023) was defined by portfolio assembly. We acquired four subsidiaries, incubated two, and established the holding company's central functions. We achieved consolidated revenue of SAR 2.1 billion in FY2023, up from SAR 680 million in FY2019 — a CAGR of 32.6%.

Our second strategic cycle (2024–2028) must be defined by portfolio optimization and value multiplication. We must shift from "collection" to "connection" — unlocking the synergies between our subsidiaries that justified their acquisition in the first place.

Three convictions underpin this strategy:

Culture is the new infrastructure. Governments and consumers are investing in cultural experiences at unprecedented rates. Our subsidiaries sit on irreplaceable cultural assets.

The holding company must earn its right to exist. Every central function, every governance mechanism, every capital allocation decision must demonstrably add value that subsidiaries could not create alone.

Digital is not a pillar — it is the atmosphere. Every subsidiary strategy must be digitally native. We will invest SAR 400 million over five years in digital transformation across the group.

Nora Al-Rashid Group CEO, Cultural Assets Group



3. WHO WE ARE — MISSION, VISION & VALUES

3.1 Mission Statement

"To preserve, activate, and scale cultural assets for the enrichment of communities and the creation of sustainable economic value."

3.2 Vision Statement

"By 2028, CAG will be the Middle East and North Africa's leading cultural economy group — recognized for the authenticity of our cultural offerings, the excellence of our operations, and the impact of our investments on communities and stakeholders."

3.3 Core Values

Value

Definition

Behavioral Anchor

Authenticity

We honor the integrity of cultural assets and never compromise heritage for short-term gain

Every product/experience must pass the "Cultural Integrity Review"

Excellence

We pursue operational and creative excellence in everything we do

Zero tolerance for mediocrity; continuous improvement embedded in KPIs

Stewardship

We are custodians, not owners, of cultural assets — we hold them in trust for future generations

Long-term value creation over short-term extraction

Collaboration

We believe the group is greater than the sum of its parts

Cross-subsidiary projects are rewarded; silos are actively dismantled

Courage

We take bold, calculated bets on the future of culture

Innovation budget ring-fenced; failure-tolerant experimentation encouraged

3.4 Strategic Identity Summary

CAG is a strategic holding company (not a financial holding or passive investor). We actively shape subsidiary strategies, allocate capital with conviction, provide shared services where scale advantages exist, and intervene when subsidiaries underperform. Our parenting style is best described as "Strategic Architect" — we set the blueprint, resource the build, and monitor progress, but we empower subsidiary CEOs to lead execution.



4. OUR THEORY OF VALUE CREATION (PARENTING PURPOSE)

4.1 The Parenting Advantage Framework

CAG creates value for its subsidiaries through five mechanisms:

#

Value Creation Mechanism

Description

Example

1

Capital Allocation

Centralized capital allocation enables investment in highest-return opportunities across the portfolio, rather than each subsidiary self-funding

SAR 120M redirected from Subsidiary 4 (mature, cash-generative) to Subsidiary 2 (high-growth, capital-hungry) in 2023

2

Talent & Leadership Development

Group-wide talent pool, leadership rotation program, and centralized executive recruitment

Group CHRO manages top-50 leadership pipeline; 3 subsidiary CEOs rotated in 2022–2023

3

Shared Services & Scale Economies

Centralized procurement, finance, legal, IT infrastructure, and marketing analytics

Group procurement saved SAR 45M in FY2023 through consolidated vendor contracts

4

Brand & Reputation Halo

The CAG brand provides credibility, government access, and partnership leverage that individual subsidiaries could not achieve alone

CAG brand enabled Subsidiary 1 to secure a 25-year government concession valued at SAR 800M

5

Strategic Synergy Orchestration

Active identification and execution of cross-subsidiary revenue and cost synergies

"Cultural Passport" product (cross-selling across Subsidiaries 1, 2, and 5) generated SAR 28M incremental revenue in FY2023

4.2 Corporate-Level Strategy

CAG's corporate-level strategy is a Related-Linked Diversification strategy. Our subsidiaries are linked by:

A common focus on cultural assets as the core resource

Shared customer segments (cultural tourists, experience seekers, government/institutional buyers)

Complementary capabilities (content creation, venue management, digital distribution, education)

Geographic overlap (primarily MENA, with selective international expansion)

We explicitly reject unrelated diversification. Any future acquisition or incubation must pass the "Cultural Nexus Test": Does this entity's core business fundamentally depend on, or contribute to, the cultural economy?

5.2 Industry Analysis — Cultural Economy Value Chain

The cultural economy value chain consists of four layers:

Cultural Asset Origination — Heritage sites, artistic creation, IP development

Cultural Asset Activation — Experiences, events, exhibitions, education

Cultural Asset Distribution — Digital platforms, media, licensing, merchandising

Cultural Asset Monetization — Ticketing, sponsorship, real estate, government contracts

CAG's portfolio spans all four layers, which is a distinctive competitive advantage. Most competitors operate in one or two layers.

• CAG demonstrates exceptionally well-articulated mission and vision statements with clear distinction between purpose (preserve, activate, scale cultural assets) and aspiration (MENA's leading cultural economy group by 2028), supported by five defined core values with behavioral anchors **[<3,019dc6ee-bd5d-7d5a-a09a-0fb846744bf8>, <4,019dc6ee-bd5e-7013-848d-cb38902ccdc7>, <8,019dc6ee-bd62-74cd-a7d0-6db503cf45c3>]**
• Strategic intent is robust with a clearly defined 5-year cycle (2024–2028), SMART financial targets (SAR 2.1B to SAR 3.6B revenue), five strategic pillars with initiative-level detail, and a deliberate shift from 'collection to connection' **[<2,019dc6ee-bd5c-7531-b65d-c051c569ce2a>, <341,019dc6ee-baa3-7ecd-b79e-3479ef298f08>]**
• The parenting purpose is among the strongest elements — CAG explicitly defines itself as a 'Strategic Architect' holding company with five documented value creation mechanisms, a 'Cultural Nexus Test' for portfolio discipline, and a Related-Linked Diversification corporate strategy **[<11,019dc6ee-bd65-73c8-b492-8fcd64f3c35f>, <12,019dc6ee-bd66-722f-a0de-4cbb7c05fbd4>, <29,019dc6ee-bd77-77e3-8a19-f6795b0d9850>]**
• A notable weakness exists in strategic coherence: the documents acknowledge synergies are 'underexploited,' holding company overhead is 'questioned by board members,' financial reporting is 'not yet consolidated in real-time,' and the dotted-line matrix between subsidiary and group functions is 'inconsistently enforced' **[<22,019dc6ee-bd70-75c4-b32d-14ae00d24cfa>, <97,019dc6ee-bdbb-7055-9368-6568b15a6fa0>]**
• The value proposition is well-positioned around full cultural value chain coverage (#1 in MENA breadth) but lacks a formal external-facing value proposition statement for customers, partners, and government stakeholders beyond competitive positioning data **[<36,019dc6ee-bd7e-7cd8-8119-67810bb51b42>, <21,019dc6ee-bd6f-7026-a27e-1a0cdea004d0>]**

• The 5-year strategic cycle (2024–2028) is clearly defined with a deliberate shift from 'portfolio assembly' (2019–2023) to 'portfolio optimization and value multiplication' **[<2,019dc6ee-bd5c-7531-b65d-c051c569ce2a>, <107,019dc6ee-b894-79ee-a946-93d8914a7bec>]**
• Financial targets are SMART: Revenue from SAR 2,100M to SAR 3,600M; EBITDA from SAR 382M to SAR 864M; EBITDA Margin from 18.2% to 24.0%; ROIC from 9.2% to 14.5%; Net Debt/EBITDA from 2.8x to 2.0x **[<341,019dc6ee-baa3-7ecd-b79e-3479ef298f08>, <437,019dc6ee-e8f3-76b6-aaae-ba5a5870aae4>]**
• Five strategic pillars are clearly defined and ranked with specific objectives: (A) Portfolio Synergy Acceleration — SAR 28M to SAR 200M synergy revenue; (B) Digital Transformation — Level 4/5 maturity by 2027; (C) Geographic Expansion — 3 new MENA markets contributing 15% revenue; (D) Operational Excellence — EBITDA margin to 24%; (E) Talent & Culture — Top 10 Employer by 2027 **[<24,019dc6ee-bd72-76b2-9799-840d780aef4c>, <40,019dc6ee-bd82-76d4-b008-881692698f5b>, <42,019dc6ee-bd84-7a3c-a981-311a140c195c>, <47,019dc6ee-bd89-7fdc-9c87-d34695c9a012>, <49,019dc6ee-bd8b-7765-ad37-8e35f244764b>]**
• Capital allocation is structured: SAR 1,950M total envelope with 61% subsidiary growth, 18% digital, 17% geographic expansion, 3% innovation **[<343,019dc6ee-baa5-7581-b051-27beb5b6f8f3>, <439,019dc6ee-e8f5-7c24-9817-5a65d07988cc>]**
• Three strategic convictions underpin the strategy: culture as new infrastructure, holding must earn right to exist, digital as atmosphere **[<2,019dc6ee-bd5c-7531-b65d-c051c569ce2a>]**
elements.evidenceQuote: Our second strategic cycle (2024–2028) must be defined by portfolio optimization and value multiplication. We must shift from 'collection' to 'connection' — unlocking the synergies between our subsidiaries that justified their acquisition in the first place.
elements.sourceDocument: Cultural Assets Group — Corporate Strategy Plan 2024–2028
elements.scoreRationale: Strategic intent is exceptionally well-defined with SMART financial targets across six metrics **[<341,019dc6ee-baa3-7ecd-b79e-3479ef298f08>]**, five prioritized strategic pillars each with initiative-level detail including owners, timelines, investments, and expected returns [1-24 through 1-49], and a SAR 1,950M capital allocation framework with governance rules **[<343,019dc6ee-baa5-7581-b051-27beb5b6f8f3>]**. The articulation of three strategic convictions and the 'collection to connection' narrative **[<2,019dc6ee-bd5c-7531-b65d-c051c569ce2a>]** demonstrates sector-leading strategic clarity.
elements.dataGap: No mid-cycle progress data available (strategy was approved January 2024); no evidence of scenario planning or contingency strategies if key assumptions fail

elements.name: Value Proposition
elements.aiAnswer:
• CAG's competitive differentiation is anchored in full cultural value chain coverage across all four layers (Origination, Activation, Distribution, Monetization) — a unique position as most competitors operate in only one or two layers **[<36,019dc6ee-bd7e-7cd8-8119-67810bb51b42>, <136,019dc6ee-b8b1-76c1-8878-2e667714d8bb>]**
• Competitive positioning is documented: #2 in MENA cultural economy by revenue (private sector); #1 in breadth of value chain coverage **[<21,019dc6ee-bd6f-7026-a27e-1a0cdea004d0>, <117,019dc6ee-b89e-7e57-b3cb-5b216f170b3a>]**
• Specific competitive advantages are articulated against five named competitors: deeper cultural authenticity vs. IMG Worlds; physical + digital presence vs. MBC Group; agility and commercial orientation vs. Diriyah Gate (government entity); cultural depth vs. Emaar Entertainment (real estate-led); portfolio breadth vs. Ithra (single-site) **[<20,019dc6ee-bd6e-7f46-9e02-d7273e8c363b>, <116,019dc6ee-b89d-71df-8d9b-b17b133d62ea>]**
• The 'Cultural Nexus Test' provides portfolio discipline: 'Does this entity's core business fundamentally depend on, or contribute to, the cultural economy?' **[<29,019dc6ee-bd77-77e3-8a19-f6795b0d9850>, <142,019dc6ee-b8b7-747e-a31c-8517fbd0b534>]**
• However, no formal external-facing value proposition statement exists for customers, partners, or government stakeholders — the value proposition is implicitly derived from competitive analysis rather than explicitly stated
elements.evidenceQuote: CAG's portfolio spans all four layers, which is a distinctive competitive advantage. Most competitors operate in one or two layers.
elements.sourceDocument: Cultural Assets Group — Corporate Strategy Plan 2024–2028
elements.scoreRationale: While competitive positioning is well-documented with specific competitor analysis **[<20,019dc6ee-bd6e-7f46-9e02-d7273e8c363b>, <21,019dc6ee-bd6f-7026-a27e-1a0cdea004d0>]** and the full value chain coverage differentiator is clearly articulated **[<36,019dc6ee-bd7e-7cd8-8119-67810bb51b42>]**, the value proposition is implicitly derived rather than explicitly stated as a formal proposition for each stakeholder segment. There is no documented customer value proposition, partner value proposition, or government stakeholder value proposition — only competitive positioning data. This represents a functional but incomplete approach.
elements.dataGap: Formal value proposition statement for each stakeholder segment (B2C consumers, B2B corporate clients, government partners, investors); customer perception data or NPS benchmarks validating the claimed differentiation

elements.name: Strategic Coherence
elements.aiAnswer:
• Strong vision-to-strategy alignment exists: the vision (MENA's leading cultural economy group) cascades into five strategic pillars, each with initiative-level detail, owners, timelines, and investment amounts [1-24 through 1-49]
• A formal strategy governance architecture is in place: Board (quarterly), GEC (bi-weekly), Investment Committee (monthly), Subsidiary Boards (quarterly), Full Group Strategy Review (semi-annual) **[<347,019dc6ee-baa9-7a7d-b76a-79467c627121>, <424,019dc6ee-e8e6-7d7a-9dd8-fc59c0ec583f>]**
• KPI cascade operates at three levels: Group (Revenue, EBITDA, ROIC, Synergy Revenue, etc.), Subsidiary (Revenue, EBITDA Margin, NPS, Talent Retention), and Initiative (milestone completion, budget variance, benefit realization) **[<351,019dc6ee-baad-7544-a368-4d171deb3221>, <426,019dc6ee-e8e8-7487-9684-d6aecf1e0541>]**
• However, the documents self-identify significant coherence gaps: 'Synergies underexploited; maturity uneven across subsidiaries; holding company overhead questioned by board members; financial reporting not yet consolidated in real-time' **[<22,019dc6ee-bd70-75c4-b32d-14ae00d24cfa>, <118,019dc6ee-b89f-7665-bd28-ea338deeaa88>]**
• The organizational structure document notes the dotted-line matrix between subsidiary functional heads and Group function heads is 'inconsistently enforced — some subsidiary Finance Directors have minimal interaction with the Group CFO' **[<97,019dc6ee-bdbb-7055-9368-6568b15a6fa0>, <314,019dc6ee-bb5c-7bda-9b72-34b0c1ecde97>]**
• Portfolio classification (BCG-inspired) with differentiated mandates (Stars, Cash Cows, Question Marks) provides strategic clarity but the cascade below VP level is not documented **[<14,019dc6ee-bd68-7651-9d6c-d4dc5f23aeec>, <122,019dc6ee-b8a3-72d9-be6d-49184ac4aec1>]**
elements.evidenceQuote: Reporting Matrix: Subsidiary functional heads (Finance, HR) have a solid line to their Subsidiary CEO and a dotted line to the corresponding Group function head. This creates a matrix that enables group standards while preserving subsidiary autonomy. However, interviews suggest the dotted line is inconsistently enforced — some subsidiary Finance Directors have minimal interaction with the Group CFO.
elements.sourceDocument: Cultural Assets Group — Group Organizational Structure
elements.scoreRationale: While the strategy-to-execution architecture is well-designed on paper with multi-level governance forums **[<347,019dc6ee-baa9-7a7d-b76a-79467c627121>]**, KPI cascades **[<351,019dc6ee-baad-7544-a368-4d171deb3221>]**, and a strategic planning calendar **[<353,019dc6ee-baaf-737c-a031-8b57acc125c6>]**, the documents themselves acknowledge material coherence gaps including underexploited synergies, uneven subsidiary maturity, questioned holding overhead, and inconsistently enforced matrix reporting **[<22,019dc6ee-bd70-75c4-b32d-14ae00d24cfa>, <97,019dc6ee-bdbb-7055-9368-6568b15a6fa0>]**. The gap between stated strategy and operational reality reduces this score to developing/adequate.
elements.dataGap: Strategy execution progress reports or balanced scorecard data showing actual vs. planned performance; evidence of functional-level strategy cascade below VP level; subsidiary-level strategy documents (referenced as Appendix B but not available)

elements.name: Parenting Purpose
elements.aiAnswer:
• CAG explicitly defines its parenting purpose through a dedicated chapter ('Our Theory of Value Creation') with five documented value creation mechanisms: (1) Capital Allocation, (2) Talent & Leadership Development, (3) Shared Services & Scale Economies, (4) Brand & Reputation Halo, (5) Strategic Synergy Orchestration **[<12,019dc6ee-bd66-722f-a0de-4cbb7c05fbd4>, <26,019dc6ee-bd74-7f01-9820-a906d4682f60>, <114,019dc6ee-b89b-7bba-811d-5a6f8b247d85>, <139,019dc6ee-b8b4-7a5a-bd31-193cd4ff1f6e>]**
• Each mechanism includes concrete examples: SAR 120M capital reallocation from Sub 4 to growth subsidiaries; 3 CEO rotations in 2022; centralized procurement in FY2023; 25-year government concession secured via CAG brand; Cultural Passport generating SAR 28M in FY2023 **[<26,019dc6ee-bd74-7f01-9820-a906d4682f60>, <139,019dc6ee-b8b4-7a5a-bd31-193cd4ff1f6e>]**
• Corporate-level strategy is explicitly defined as 'Related-Linked Diversification' with four linkage dimensions: common cultural asset focus, shared customer segments, complementary capabilities, geographic overlap **[<28,019dc6ee-bd76-7c90-9c78-0d6ed5b59337>, <29,019dc6ee-bd77-77e3-8a19-f6795b0d9850>, <141,019dc6ee-b8b6-7fc6-8446-4730879e7d2d>, <142,019dc6ee-b8b7-747e-a31c-8517fbd0b534>]**
• The 'Cultural Nexus Test' provides acquisition discipline: 'Does this entity's core business fundamentally depend on, or contribute to, the cultural economy?' with explicit rejection of unrelated diversification **[<29,019dc6ee-bd77-77e3-8a19-f6795b0d9850>, <142,019dc6ee-b8b7-747e-a31c-8517fbd0b534>]**
• The parenting style is named as 'Strategic Architect' — 'we set the blueprint, resource the build, and monitor progress, but we empower subsidiary CEOs to lead execution' **[<11,019dc6ee-bd65-73c8-b492-8fcd64f3c35f>, <113,019dc6ee-b89a-7bb7-800a-48c6fc4d0724>]**
• The Group CEO explicitly states: 'The holding company must earn its right to exist. Every central function, every governance mechanism, every capital allocation decision must demonstrably add value that subsidiaries could not create alone' **[<2,019dc6ee-bd5c-7531-b65d-c051c569ce2a>, <107,019dc6ee-b894-79ee-a946-93d8914a7bec>]**
elements.evidenceQuote: CAG is a strategic holding company (not a financial holding or passive investor). We actively shape subsidiary strategies, allocate capital with conviction, provide shared services where scale advantages exist, and intervene when subsidiaries underperform. Our parenting style is best described as 'Strategic Architect' — we set the blueprint, resource the build, and monitor progress, but we empower subsidiary CEOs to lead execution.
elements.sourceDocument: Cultural Assets Group — Corporate Strategy Plan 2024–2028
elements.scoreRationale: The parenting purpose is sector-leading in its articulation. CAG dedicates an entire strategy chapter to its theory of value creation **[<12,019dc6ee-bd66-722f-a0de-4cbb7c05fbd4>]**, names five specific mechanisms with concrete examples **[<26,019dc6ee-bd74-7f01-9820-a906d4682f60>, <139,019dc6ee-b8b4-7a5a-bd31-193cd4ff1f6e>]**, explicitly defines its corporate-level strategy as Related-Linked Diversification **[<28,019dc6ee-bd76-7c90-9c78-0d6ed5b59337>]**, establishes the 'Cultural Nexus Test' for portfolio discipline **[<29,019dc6ee-bd77-77e3-8a19-f6795b0d9850>]**, and the CEO's conviction that 'the holding company must earn its right to exist' **[<2,019dc6ee-bd5c-7531-b65d-c051c569ce2a>]** demonstrates exceptional self-awareness. The 'Strategic Architect' label with clear behavioral definition **[<11,019dc6ee-bd65-73c8-b492-8fcd64f3c35f>]** is best-in-class for GCC holding companies.
elements.dataGap: Quantified parenting value-add (e.g., total SAR value created by holding vs. cost of holding overhead of SAR 42M); subsidiary CEO satisfaction survey on holding company value-add; evidence of the 'Cultural Nexus Test' being applied to reject a potential acquisition

strengths: Exceptionally well-articulated mission, vision, values, and parenting purpose with dedicated strategy chapter and five named value creation mechanisms — rare for a cultural economy holding company in MENA **[<3,019dc6ee-bd5d-7d5a-a09a-0fb846744bf8>, <8,019dc6ee-bd62-74cd-a7d0-6db503cf45c3>, <12,019dc6ee-bd66-722f-a0de-4cbb7c05fbd4>, <26,019dc6ee-bd74-7f01-9820-a906d4682f60>]**

Full cultural value chain coverage across all four layers (Origination, Activation, Distribution, Monetization) with #1 breadth position in MENA — a structural competitive advantage that competitors cannot easily replicate **[<36,019dc6ee-bd7e-7cd8-8119-67810bb51b42>, <136,019dc6ee-b8b1-76c1-8878-2e667714d8bb>]**

SMART financial targets with clear 5-year trajectory (SAR 2.1B to SAR 3.6B revenue, 18.2% to 24.0% EBITDA margin) and a disciplined SAR 1,950M capital allocation framework with governance rules **[<341,019dc6ee-baa3-7ecd-b79e-3479ef298f08>, <343,019dc6ee-baa5-7581-b051-27beb5b6f8f3>]**

Strong portfolio management discipline with BCG-inspired classification (3 Stars, 2 Cash Cows, 1 Question Mark), differentiated mandates, and the 'Cultural Nexus Test' preventing unrelated diversification **[<14,019dc6ee-bd68-7651-9d6c-d4dc5f23aeec>, <29,019dc6ee-bd77-77e3-8a19-f6795b0d9850>]**

Self-aware leadership that explicitly acknowledges the holding must 'earn its right to exist' and identifies its own weaknesses (underexploited synergies, uneven maturity, questioned overhead) **[<2,019dc6ee-bd5c-7531-b65d-c051c569ce2a>, <22,019dc6ee-bd70-75c4-b32d-14ae00d24cfa>]**
weaknesses: Strategic coherence gap between stated strategy and operational reality: synergies underexploited (only SAR 28M in FY2023 vs. SAR 200M target), matrix reporting inconsistently enforced, financial reporting not consolidated in real-time **[<22,019dc6ee-bd70-75c4-b32d-14ae00d24cfa>, <97,019dc6ee-bdbb-7055-9368-6568b15a6fa0>]**

No formal external-facing value proposition statement for customers, partners, or government stakeholders — competitive differentiation is documented but not translated into stakeholder-specific value propositions **[<20,019dc6ee-bd6e-7f46-9e02-d7273e8c363b>, <21,019dc6ee-bd6f-7026-a27e-1a0cdea004d0>]**

Holding company overhead questioned by board members, and the Group CEO's span of control (12 direct reports) is at the upper limit of effectiveness **[<22,019dc6ee-bd70-75c4-b32d-14ae00d24cfa>, <97,019dc6ee-bdbb-7055-9368-6568b15a6fa0>]**

Relatively new leadership team (GEC average tenure 3.0 years, Group CMO and CTO both at 1 year) creates execution risk for an ambitious 5-year strategy **[<97,019dc6ee-bdbb-7055-9368-6568b15a6fa0>, <377,019dc6ee-bac7-7c90-8b3d-ba89f8d29f19>]**
opportunities: Saudi Vision 2030 allocating SAR 50B+ to culture and entertainment creates a massive tailwind, and CAG's strong government relationships (MoC and PIF board representatives) position it to capture disproportionate share **[<32,019dc6ee-bd7a-75c0-b83e-3aa463f22389>, <59,019dc6ee-bd95-71d6-a9fc-b646ae94476c>]**

Cross-subsidiary synergy revenue target of SAR 200M by 2028 (from SAR 28M baseline) represents a 7x growth opportunity that validates the holding structure if achieved **[<24,019dc6ee-bd72-76b2-9799-840d780aef4c>, <120,019dc6ee-b8a1-7572-a521-cf54fc18dfd6>]**

Geographic expansion into Egypt, Morocco, and Turkey with SAR 340M allocated could establish CAG as the first pan-MENA cultural economy group **[<42,019dc6ee-bd84-7a3c-a981-311a140c195c>, <43,019dc6ee-bd85-775d-aba3-560fbc5ee363>, <46,019dc6ee-bd88-73ac-a1a8-29d4aa993836>]**

Digital transformation investment of SAR 400M over five years, including AI-powered cultural experiences and digital twins, could create new revenue streams and competitive moats **[<2,019dc6ee-bd5c-7531-b65d-c051c569ce2a>, <40,019dc6ee-bd82-76d4-b008-881692698f5b>, <41,019dc6ee-bd83-7999-877b-151e170a2756>]**
threats: Government entities (Diriyah Gate, Ithra) competing directly with SAR 3.0B+ in government funding, potentially crowding out private-sector players like CAG **[<20,019dc6ee-bd6e-7f46-9e02-d7273e8c363b>, <22,019dc6ee-bd70-75c4-b32d-14ae00d24cfa>]**

Talent war for creative and tech professionals in a market where Sub 3 (Digital Content) has only 55% Saudization rate due to tech talent scarcity **[<97,019dc6ee-bdbb-7055-9368-6568b15a6fa0>, <314,019dc6ee-bb5c-7bda-9b72-34b0c1ecde97>]**

Economic downturn risk reducing discretionary cultural spending, with CAG's revenue heavily dependent on consumer and government cultural investment **[<22,019dc6ee-bd70-75c4-b32d-14ae00d24cfa>, <44,019dc6ee-bd86-7261-963d-3c04478601fc>]**

Digital transformation execution failure risk rated Medium likelihood / High impact, with SAR 400M at stake across a group with uneven digital maturity **[<44,019dc6ee-bd86-7261-963d-3c04478601fc>, <152,019dc6ee-b8c1-7a9e-a723-09e2d18ddeb8>]**

leadership: [Mission & Vision Clarity] — The mission statement references 'enrichment of communities' alongside 'sustainable economic value' **[<3,019dc6ee-bd5d-7d5a-a09a-0fb846744bf8>]**. When these two objectives conflict — for example, when a heritage site's commercial exploitation threatens its cultural integrity — what decision framework does the Board use to adjudicate, and can you cite a specific instance where this tension was resolved?

P2.name: Governance & Leadership
P2.description: How is the entity governed and led?

execSummary.aiDraft:
• CAG has a well-structured 9-member Board with 4 independent directors, 2 government representatives, and 3 executives, supported by 4 board committees (Audit & Risk, Nomination & Remuneration, Investment, Strategy) **[<20,019dc6ee-badb-7d90-8013-2499c4370048>, <140,019dc6ee-c033-7725-b69a-1929f50931f9>, <261,019dc6ee-b96f-73d3-ac8f-859883fb05e4>]**
• The Group Executive Committee (GEC) comprises 7 experienced C-suite leaders with strong private-sector backgrounds (McKinsey, PwC, Accenture, AWS, Baker McKenzie), though average tenure is only 3.0 years and 2 members (CMO, CTO) have been in role for just 1 year **[<15,019dc6ee-bad6-7a45-b9ec-8dcd97fea7b8>, <135,019dc6ee-c02e-758d-9e95-92994d11e952>, <238,019dc6ee-b958-71f0-a446-fa586dd41720>]**
• Decision-making architecture is clearly tiered with defined forums (Board quarterly, GEC bi-weekly, Investment Committee monthly, Subsidiary Boards quarterly, Strategy Review semi-annual) and a documented capital allocation governance framework with explicit approval thresholds **[<329,019dc6ee-e9b9-72a6-ab3f-3ff4e10a2720>, <324,019dc6ee-e9b4-764d-9bfd-f4224b3ee22a>, <325,019dc6ee-e9b5-7a55-a58a-d3dbd82d28cb>]**
• KPI cascade exists at Group, Subsidiary, and Initiative levels with defined review cadences, but no evidence of formal consequence management for missed targets or individual executive performance scorecards **[<128,019dc6ee-c027-7be6-92a7-efe90d89d4b0>, <297,019dc6ee-e999-7c85-82c7-eaaca50ddd6c>]**
• Parenting style is explicitly articulated as 'Strategic Architect' with 5 documented value creation mechanisms, but the matrix reporting structure between holding and subsidiaries is acknowledged as inconsistently enforced **[<124,019dc6ee-c023-7eb7-9ef1-9b067ac4f438>, <150,019dc6ee-c03d-7c61-ae23-61236090991e>, <389,019dc6ee-e9f5-79d2-a2a4-a917df71ecf4>]**
